processes.name: Annual workforce & headcount plan
processes.summary: Turns the board-approved operating plan into a funded headcount plan by function, level, location and worker type for the next fiscal year, with quarterly re-forecasts. Scope covers all employees and budgeted contingent workers across the US, Canada, India, Taiwan and China. Good looks like one version of the truth in Darwinbox position management, reconciled to FP&A's model, with location choices that already reflect export-control, immigration and local labor-law constraints.
processes.owner: FP&A (budget and model), HRBPs (workforce content), CHRO (sign-off with CFO)
processes.trigger: FP&A annual operating plan calendar (kick-off typically in Q3 for the next fiscal year), or a material mid-year re-forecast
outputs: Approved headcount plan by cost center, job family, level, location and worker type
Budgeted positions pre-created in Darwinbox with budget line IDs
Location/hub strategy memo (export-control, immigration and cost rationale)
Quarterly hiring cadence feeding the TA capacity plan
Baseline workforce data set reused for the 10-K human capital section
processes.sla: Plan locked 30 days before fiscal year start; quarterly re-forecast within 10 business days of quarter close

steps.label: Issue planning calendar and cost envelopes
steps.detail: FP&A publishes the opex envelope per function and fully loaded cost-per-head by location: base, bonus, equity burn, employer social charges (e.g., China housing fund, India EPF on the new INR 25,000 ceiling, Canada CPP/CPP2/EI, Taiwan labor insurance and 6% pension) and deadlines.

steps.label: Publish baseline headcount and attrition
steps.detail: Snapshot Darwinbox as of a fixed date: filled positions, open reqs, accepted-not-started offers, contingent workers from the PL-05 register, and trailing 12-month attrition by function and location. Freeze definitions (headcount vs FTE, interns, long-term leave) so the numbers tie to later disclosure.

steps.label: Build bottom-up role demand
steps.detail: Each Dept Head submits incremental roles tied to the product roadmap (tape-outs, new nodes, customer programs), with job family and level from PL-03, preferred location, worker type and quarter of need, and flags roles that will touch controlled technology or source code.

steps.label: Screen location mix for export limits
steps.detail: Trade Compliance reviews roles planned for China, Taiwan, India and Canada R&D sites and foreign-person-heavy teams: which technologies (e.g., 3A090/4A090-type advanced computing, advanced-node design) can be worked on where, and likely license lead times. Output is a location constraint list, not a nationality rule.

steps.label: Stress-test talent supply and legal limits
steps.detail: HRBPs test feasibility: H-1B timing and cost (March wage-weighted lottery; $100K payment vacated but re-proclaimed; proposed $103,265 cap-petition fee for FY2028), Canada GTS as a fallback, China dispatch at or under 10%, India worker/non-worker mix, and Taiwan overtime cost. They propose hub alternatives where supply or rules make a location unrealistic.

steps.label: Within opex envelope?
steps.detail: FP&A consolidates demand at location cost and compares it with the envelope, including contingent spend and equity burn.

steps.label: Re-prioritize or relocate roles
steps.detail: Dept Heads cut, defer or relocate roles and name the trade-offs explicitly; any proposed reductions are routed to PL-04/OF-03 under Legal privilege rather than being written into shared planning files.

steps.label: Approve plan with CFO and CEO
steps.detail: CHRO and CFO sign the plan; the CEO approves and the board receives a summary. Planned reductions, if any, get a separate WARN/Cal-WARN, China Art. 41, Taiwan Mass Redundancy and ON/BC group-notice analysis before anything is communicated.

steps.label: Load positions and publish dashboards
steps.detail: The approved plan is loaded as budgeted positions with budget line IDs in Darwinbox; the plan-vs-actual dashboard refreshes monthly and becomes the reference for PL-02 requisition approval.
steps.control: Loaded positions reconciled to FP&A model by cost center before go-live

steps.label: Plan locked; quarterly re-forecast
steps.detail: Plan is version-locked; FP&A reopens it only at quarterly re-forecast or on a CFO-declared event (e.g., hiring freeze, acquisition).

raci.activity: Set opex envelope and cost-per-head assumptions
Bottom-up role demand by location and level

controls.control: Approved plan headcount and cost reconcile to the FP&A model by cost center before positions are loaded
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation workbook (Darwinbox budgeted positions vs FP&A model) with CHRO and CFO sign-off

controls.control: Every planned role in a China, Taiwan, India or Canada R&D location is reviewed by Trade Compliance for technology scope before approval
controls.evidence: Location screening log with Trade Compliance sign-off

controls.control: Monthly plan-vs-actual variance review; variances over 2% or 5 heads per function are explained
controls.evidence: Monthly variance report with FP&A and HRBP commentary

kpis.name: Headcount plan accuracy
kpis.why: Shows the plan is a real control, not a wish list.

kpis.name: Hiring plan attainment
kpis.target: >=90% of planned hires started in the planned quarter
kpis.why: Links TA capacity and approval speed to delivery.

kpis.name: Cost-per-head variance
kpis.why: Catches bad location assumptions (equity, social charges, FX) early.

considerations: Plan in positions, not heads: pre-creating budgeted positions in Darwinbox turns PL-02 approval into a lookup and gives the monthly SOX-light reconciliation a single key.

Price locations honestly: a Shanghai or Hsinchu engineer may cost less, but if the role needs technology that requires a license for the likely talent pool, the real cost includes license lead time or a narrower role.

Treat immigration as a budget line: US new-grad hiring that depends on H-1B cap selection converts at roughly lottery odds, so plan Canada GTS or Asia-hub alternates rather than assuming every US offer lands.

Keep any planned reductions out of shared planning files until Legal has cleared WARN, Cal-WARN, China Art. 41, Taiwan Mass Redundancy and ON/BC group-notice analysis; leaked plans become litigation evidence and can be MNPI.
Put contingent labor in the plan as its own worker type so total workforce cost is visible and China dispatch stays under the 10% cap.
Reuse the frozen baseline date and definitions for the 10-K human capital section so disclosed figures tie to HRIS evidence.

variations.when: Mid-year re-forecast after a revenue miss
variations.how: FP&A issues a revised envelope; open reqs freeze by default and must be re-justified; accepted offers are honored; any reductions go to PL-04/OF-03.
Acquired headcount is loaded as a separate plan layer with its own cost-center mapping; jobs are mapped to the architecture (PL-03) within 90 days; retention grants are budgeted separately.
Plan includes entity setup lead time, an EOR bridge if needed (PL-05), payroll registration and local mandatory policies before the first hire date.

countries.us: Each new remote work state triggers payroll registration, state notices and pay-transparency posting rules, and reductions can trigger federal WARN (100+ employees, 60 days) or NY/NJ 90-day mini-WARN. Budget FY2028 H-1B scenarios (proposed $103,265 cap-petition fee) and note that the Sept 18, 2026 EO makes past-year and planned layoffs a factor in H-1B/LCA adjudication.
countries.us-ca: Map planned job codes to the 23 SOC-based categories required from the 2027 CRD pay data report (due 12 May 2027), and budget non-exempt lab roles with daily overtime or at the exempt floor ($72,384 from 2027). Cal-WARN applies to mass layoffs of 50+ in 30 days at a covered establishment (75+ employees).
countries.ca: Load Canadian costs with 2026 CPP/CPP2/EI rates and provincial Employer Health Tax, and tag engineering roles for SR&ED time coding so credits are supportable. BC employers with 50+ employees publish their first gender pay-gap report by Nov 1, 2026, so planned level and pay mix will be visible.
countries.in: Cost CTC on the Labour Codes' 50% 'wages' base and the INR 25,000 EPF ceiling (from 17 Sep 2026), and track 'worker' headcount because standing orders apply at 300+ workers and a Grievance Redressal Committee at 20+. A hardware lab with 20+ workers using power can become a 'factory' under the OSH Code.
countries.tw: Budget the 2027 minimum wage (set in Q3 for 1 Jan 2027), overtime for LSA-covered engineers (there is no salary-based exemption) and profit-sharing competition from TSMC and MediaTek. Flag roles touching national core key technologies (e.g., AI/HPC chip design, chiplet interconnect) for security vetting and mainland-travel approval rules.
countries.cn: Budget social insurance and housing fund on actual wages within the city base (Shanghai RMB 7,546-37,731 from 1 Jul 2026) plus 2% union funds; Shanghai and Shenzhen differ on minimum wage, leave and sick pay. Keep dispatched workers at or below 10% of the workforce and plan contract end dates around the rising statutory retirement ages.

processes.name: Requisition & position approval
processes.summary: Controls how a need becomes an open, postable requisition: every req maps to a budgeted Darwinbox position, has a validated job code, level, location and pay range, and carries an export-control classification before it reaches Greenhouse. Covers backfills and net-new roles, including fixed-term hires, in all six jurisdictions. Good looks like in-plan approvals in 5 business days, zero reqs opened outside the plan, and a monthly headcount-to-budget reconciliation that FP&A and People Ops both sign.
processes.owner: HRBP (process), FP&A (budget control), People Ops (position management), Trade Compliance (role classification)
processes.trigger: A vacancy from a resignation or termination (backfill), or a planned or unplanned net-new need raised by a hiring manager
outputs: Approved T-REQ with budget line ID and full approval trail
Active Darwinbox position record (position ID, job code, grade, location, cost center, export flag)
Greenhouse job opened with approved pay range, hiring team and interview plan
Export-control role classification record from Trade Compliance
Monthly headcount-vs-budget reconciliation signed by FP&A and People Ops
processes.sla: 5 business days submission-to-open for in-plan reqs; 10 business days for out-of-plan exceptions

steps.label: Identify vacancy or new need
steps.detail: Manager confirms the business need: a vacancy from OF-01/OF-02 or a roadmap-driven role. For backfills, first ask whether the role should be re-scoped, re-leveled, relocated or eliminated; backfill is not automatic.

steps.label: Submit T-REQ in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Complete T-REQ: position ID (or 'new'), job code and level from the job architecture, work location (city/state, or remote with eligible states/provinces), cost center, worker type and contract term, backfill vs net-new, target start, plan line and justification, hiring team, and whether the role will access controlled technology or source code.

steps.label: Validate job code, level and location
steps.detail: HRBP checks job code and level against the PL-03 leveling guide and team peers, confirms the location is an approved hiring location (entity and payroll registered), pulls the pay range for the location from the comp planning tool, and records overtime status (FLSA/CA exempt, ON/BC exemption, India worker vs non-worker).

steps.label: Backfill or net-new?
steps.detail: Backfill means the req refills an existing budgeted position ID; anything else is net-new.

steps.label: Confirm vacated position is funded
steps.detail: People Ops confirms the vacated position is still budgeted, not frozen or already refilled, and that the backfill is same-or-lower level in the same cost center. A change in level, location or cost center is treated as net-new for budget purposes.
steps.control: Like-for-like backfills only; any change re-routes to full FP&A review

steps.label: Check against budget and plan line
steps.detail: FP&A verifies the req maps to an open budgeted position or approved PL-01 plan line, that fully loaded cost at the range midpoint fits the cost center's remaining budget, and that start-quarter timing matches the plan.
steps.control: Hard stop: no req proceeds without a budget line ID or approved exception

steps.label: Within approved budget?
steps.detail: In-plan reqs go straight to classification; out-of-plan reqs need a funding source.

steps.label: Approve out-of-plan exception
steps.detail: Exceptions must name a funding source: an offset (a named position closed or frozen) within the Dept Head's org, or incremental budget approved by CFO and CHRO; incremental Director+ or above-threshold roles also need CEO approval. Rationale is recorded on the T-REQ.

steps.label: Classify role's technology access
steps.detail: Trade Compliance and the manager classify whether the position will access EAR/ITAR-controlled technology or source code (e.g., 3E001-type design technology, encryption source) and set the export flag on the position. Flagged positions trigger TA-06 after offer and drive I-129 Part 6 answers; a 'US citizens only' requirement is never set without a documented legal or contract basis.

steps.label: Final approval per matrix
steps.detail: Darwinbox routes by rule: like-for-like backfill = Manager + Dept Head; in-plan net-new = Dept Head + HRBP; Director and above adds CHRO; VP+ and officer roles add CEO (and TA-09). The requester can never approve their own req.

steps.label: Create or activate the position
steps.detail: People Ops creates or activates the Darwinbox position linking position ID, budget line ID, job code, grade, location, cost center and export flag; status moves to 'Open - Approved'.
steps.control: SoD: People Ops cannot approve reqs; requesters have no position-management rights

steps.label: Open job in Greenhouse
steps.detail: The Darwinbox-Greenhouse integration creates the job from the active position; the Recruiter confirms posting range (TA-01), hiring team and interview plan with scorecard (TA-03), and books the intake meeting.

steps.label: Reconcile positions to budget monthly
steps.detail: FP&A and People Ops reconcile Darwinbox filled and open positions, Greenhouse open jobs and accepted offers to budget by cost center, and investigate any Greenhouse job without an active position or any hire into an unbudgeted position.
steps.control: SOX-light headcount-vs-budget reconciliation with named preparer and reviewer

steps.label: Req open and reconciled
steps.detail: Requisition is live in Greenhouse, tied to a funded position and included in the monthly reconciliation.

steps.label: Req declined; need closed
steps.detail: Manager is notified with the reason; a vacated position is marked frozen or eliminated in Darwinbox and FP&A releases or re-allocates the budget.

raci.activity: Validate job code, level, location and pay range

controls.control: A req cannot be submitted for approval without a budget line ID or an approved exception (Darwinbox mandatory field and workflow rule)
controls.evidence: Darwinbox workflow configuration export and approval audit trail

controls.control: Approval matrix enforced in workflow by level, org and budget status; the requester cannot approve their own req
controls.evidence: Workflow rule export; quarterly SoD access review (DS-04)

controls.control: Positions are created only from approved reqs, and Greenhouse jobs only from active Darwinbox positions
controls.evidence: Integration log; weekly exception report of Greenhouse jobs without a position ID

controls.control: Monthly reconciliation of positions, open jobs and accepted offers to budget by cost center; every unbudgeted head is investigated
controls.evidence: Signed reconciliation workbook (FP&A preparer, People Ops reviewer) retained per records schedule

controls.control: Export flag set by Trade Compliance before the job opens; flagged roles cannot carry citizenship restrictions without a documented legal or contract basis
controls.evidence: Classification record in the export-control screening tool; posting review log

controls.control: Quarterly sample audit of approved reqs for correct job code, level, location and pay range
controls.evidence: Audit sample sheet with remediation log

kpis.name: Req approval cycle time
kpis.target: Median <=5 business days in-plan; <=10 for exceptions
kpis.why: Slow approvals lose candidates; fast in-plan approvals are the payoff for good planning.

kpis.name: Unbudgeted hires
kpis.why: Direct measure of the headcount-vs-budget control.

kpis.name: Out-of-plan exception rate
kpis.why: A high rate means PL-01 is unrealistic or the process is being bypassed.

kpis.name: Req data accuracy
kpis.target: >=98% of sampled reqs correct on job code, level, location and range
kpis.why: Errors flow into pay-transparency postings, offers and pay-equity cohorts.

kpis.name: Backfill challenge rate
kpis.target: Tracked; 20-30% of backfills re-scoped, relocated or eliminated
kpis.why: Shows vacancies are being challenged, not rubber-stamped.

considerations: Make the position, not the req, the unit of control: a req is a request to fill a budgeted position ID, which makes backfills trivial, net-new visible and the monthly reconciliation a simple join.
Do not auto-approve backfills. A mandatory 're-scope, relocate, re-level or eliminate?' question on every vacancy is the cheapest workforce-cost lever available.

Set the pay range at req stage, not at posting: CA, CO, WA, NY, ON, BC and others require ranges in postings, and agreeing the range before sourcing prevents range creep and pay-equity problems later.
Scale approval thresholds with cost and precedent, not title alone: a first Director role in a new country is riskier than a like-for-like senior engineer backfill.

Classify export sensitivity once per position and re-check on change, rather than per candidate; keeping the flag need-based (technology access) is also what keeps you clear of 8 U.S.C. 1324b citizenship discrimination.
Keep the SOX-light control light: one monthly reconciliation with a named preparer and reviewer is auditable; ten approvers per req is delay, not control.
Evergreen reqs (new-grad pools, FAE pipelines) should map to a capped count of positions, never an open-ended budget.
Require every out-of-plan approval to name the offset so exceptions do not silently raise the run-rate.
Watch contract-term labels in Asia: ongoing roles must be indefinite-term in Taiwan, and in China the contract term sets the probation maximum and the path to an open-ended contract.

variations.when: Like-for-like backfill (same job code, level, location, cost center)
variations.how: Fast track: Manager + Dept Head only; the FP&A check is systemic because the position is already funded; target 2 business days.

Req flagged confidential with restricted visibility in Darwinbox and Greenhouse; HRBP and Legal approve; no public posting until the exit is communicated, and pay-range rules apply once anything is posted.
Route to TA-09: CEO approval, Comp Committee visibility, 8-K and Section 16 planning; position cost modeled with equity at grant value.
One req covers a capped number of positions (e.g., 20 new-grad design engineers); each hire consumes a position; FP&A reviews the cap quarterly; TA-08 applies.

variations.when: Role in a new location or country without an entity
variations.how: People Ops confirms entity and payroll registration or an EOR bridge (PL-05) before approval; Legal confirms local contract and posting rules.
Budget and approval still required; Ontario internal-only postings are outside the ESA posting rules, but Virginia requires ranges in internal postings and several states reach promotion notices.
FP&A sets affected cost centers to 'freeze'; only CEO-approved critical roles proceed; accepted offers are honored.

countries.us: Capture the work state on every req, because pay-range posting laws reach roles that may be filled in CO, WA, NY, IL, MN, MD, NJ, VT, MA, VA (Jul 1, 2026), ME (Jul 29, 2026) and CT (Oct 1, 2026), often including remote roles. Set exempt/non-exempt status at req stage (federal $684/week salary test plus duties; higher state thresholds). If the role will likely need H-1B sponsorship, record it so cost scenarios (wage-weighted lottery, proposed $103,265 cap-petition fee for FY2028) are visible to approvers.
countries.us-ca: The req range becomes the SB 642 'good-faith estimate' of the pay the company reasonably expects to pay at hire (LC 432.3), so a range wider than real practice is itself a risk. Verify exempt status against the $70,304 floor (2026; $72,384 in 2027) and California's stricter duties tests; lab technicians are usually non-exempt. Tag job codes to the SOC-based categories needed for the 2027 pay data report.
countries.ca: For Ontario (25+ employees) the req must record whether the vacancy currently exists, because public postings must say so, and the posted range can have a spread of no more than C$50,000 (roles over C$200,000 exempt). BC public postings need a pay range. Confirm the ON information-technology-professional or BC high-technology-professional overtime exemption role by role, and route any Quebec remote req to Legal (French documents, OQLF registration at 25+).
countries.in: Classify each req as 'worker' or managerial/supervisory based on dominant duties (supervisor pay ceiling INR 18,000/month), because this drives retrenchment rights, standing orders at 300+ workers and the Grievance Redressal Committee. Budget CTC on the 50% 'wages' definition and the INR 25,000 EPF ceiling from 17 Sep 2026. Vacancies must be reported to the National Career Service before filling under the Social Security Code rules.
countries.tw: Reqs for ongoing work must be indefinite-term; fixed-term contracts are limited to temporary or short-term (up to 6 months), seasonal (up to 9 months) or specific work (LSA Art. 9). Budget overtime because Taiwan has no salary-based exemption, and flag roles in national core key technology areas for clean-hire and travel-approval handling. Postings for roles paying under NT$40,000/month must show a salary range.
countries.cn: Specify the contract term on the req because it sets the maximum probation (1, 2 or 6 months) and the route to an open-ended contract after two consecutive fixed terms. Labor dispatch reqs are limited to temporary, auxiliary or substitute positions within the 10% cap. Choose Shanghai or Shenzhen deliberately: social insurance bases, minimum wage and leave rules differ.

processes.name: Job architecture & leveling
processes.summary: Maintains the global job catalog (functions, job families, levels, job codes) and the leveling guide that every req, offer, promotion and pay range references. Covers new and changed job codes, periodic audits and regulatory category mapping across all entities. Good looks like one Darwinbox catalog mapped to salary structures, overtime status and reporting categories, with no one-off titles.
processes.owner: Total Rewards (architecture owner), HRBPs (application), HR Analytics (data), Legal (classification)
processes.trigger: Annual architecture review, a new or changed role request, M&A integration, or a regulatory change (e.g., new pay data categories)
outputs: Global job catalog in Darwinbox (job codes, families, levels)
Leveling guide with level descriptors and career paths
Job code mapping to salary ranges, overtime status and regulatory categories
Change log with approvals
Country title conventions
processes.sla: New or changed job code resolved within 10 business days; full catalog audit annually

steps.label: Request new or changed job code
steps.detail: Manager submits a Darwinbox form with role purpose, key responsibilities, closest existing job, scope (team, budget, technical complexity) and locations.

steps.label: Map to existing catalog first
steps.detail: HRBP tries to map the request to an existing job code and level; most requests are title preferences, not new jobs.

steps.label: Existing job code fits?
steps.detail: If an existing code covers at least ~80% of the duties at the right level, use it.

steps.label: Evaluate and level the role
steps.detail: Level against the guide's factors (scope, complexity, autonomy, impact, knowledge), benchmark to survey jobs (semiconductor cuts) for pricing, place it in a family and define the career path.

steps.label: Set overtime and legal classification
steps.detail: Set per-country status: US FLSA and CA exempt tests; ON/BC IT exemptions; India worker vs non-worker; Taiwan LSA coverage (Art. 84-1 only for designated roles); China standard vs approved special hours; non-compete eligibility.

steps.label: Approve code and assign ranges
steps.detail: Architecture committee approves; the code is created with geo-zone ranges and logged in the change log with version and effective date.

steps.label: Load code and map report categories
steps.detail: Load into Darwinbox and map EEO-1 category (while still required), CA SOC-based pay data category, 10-K human capital categories and any local statutory category.

steps.label: Communicate mapping to manager
steps.detail: HRBP explains the mapping, level and range, and updates the req or employee record.

steps.label: Job code active in catalog
steps.detail: Code is live and selectable in Darwinbox and Greenhouse picklists.

raci.activity: Maintain job catalog and leveling guide
Overtime and legal classification per country

controls.control: New job codes require documented leveling rationale and Legal classification before activation
controls.evidence: Job code change log with approvals

controls.control: Annual sample audit of incumbents' duties vs job code, focused on exempt/worker edge cases
controls.evidence: Audit report and reclassification actions

controls.control: Titles in offers and promotions must come from the catalog (Darwinbox picklist, no free text)
controls.evidence: System configuration export

kpis.name: Incumbents in benchmarked job codes
kpis.why: Unbenchmarked codes cannot be priced or defended.

kpis.name: Single-incumbent job codes
kpis.why: One-off codes defeat pay-equity cohorts and invite title inflation.

kpis.name: Open misclassification findings
kpis.why: Overtime misclassification is the costliest architecture error.

considerations: Separate level from title: lock the level and let country title conventions vary (Taiwan and China titles often read one level higher in the local market).
Overtime status belongs to job code plus location, not level: a lab technician code is non-exempt in California, and every engineer in Taiwan is LSA-covered.
Keep architecture stable; use career-path notes rather than new codes for niches (DFT, analog layout, SI/PI) so pay-equity cohorts stay large enough to analyze.
Equal-pay laws compare 'substantially similar work', so codes that lump dissimilar work, or split similar work, create exposure.
Map non-compete eligibility to levels in China (senior management and senior technical staff) and to trade-secret access in Taiwan so restrictive covenants are issued only where valid.

variations.how: Map acquired jobs within 90 days; red- or green-circle pay instead of forcing moves; in Canada watch constructive dismissal if titles or duties shrink.
Add local title conventions and statutory classifications before the first hire.

variations.when: Regulatory category change (e.g., CA 23 SOC categories from the 2027 report)
variations.how: HR Analytics remaps all codes; Legal signs off the mapping before the snapshot period.

countries.us: Assign FLSA exempt status per job code ($684/week salary plus duties; HCE $107,432) and track higher state thresholds (CA, NY, WA, CO). Keep EEO-1 job categories mapped until the EEOC's proposed rescission is final.
countries.us-ca: Classify against the $70,304 (2026) salary floor and California duties tests; the computer-professional exemption ($58.85/hr) fits software and EDA roles, not hardware design as such. SB 642 extends Equal Pay Act 'wages' to bonuses, stock and benefits, so family and level design underpins equal-pay defenses.
countries.ca: Confirm the ON information-technology-professional and BC high-technology-professional overtime exemptions role by role; technicians and support staff often do not qualify. Keep job classes clean for Ontario Pay Equity Act comparisons (verify plan obligations).
countries.in: Record dominant duties so each job code has a documented 'worker' vs managerial/supervisory status (supervisor ceiling INR 18,000/month); individual-contributor engineers are often workers under the Labour Codes.
countries.tw: There is no salary-based exemption: engineers and most managers are LSA-covered unless a role is MOL-designated under Art. 84-1 with an approved agreement, and only true mandated managers under the Company Act fall outside the LSA.
countries.cn: Roles on comprehensive or flexible (non-fixed) hour systems need local HR bureau approval, so flag them in the catalog. Tag levels eligible for non-competes (senior management, senior technical staff with trade-secret access).

processes.name: Organization design change
processes.summary: Governs reorganizations, spans-and-layers changes, team moves and location consolidations from design through legal checks, employee-representative consultation and effective-dated HRIS changes. Scope runs from a manager swap to a multi-country restructure; any role eliminations hand off to OF-03. Good looks like a documented business case, consultation and notice triggers identified before anything is announced, and HRIS changes that keep approvals, access, export licenses and immigration filings aligned.
processes.owner: HRBP (process), Dept Head (design), Legal and Employee Relations (consultation and risk)
processes.trigger: A leader proposes a structure change: new or merged teams, changed reporting lines, location moves, spans/layers redesign or role eliminations
outputs: Business case with current and future org charts
People impact assessment (roles changed or eliminated, locations, visas, export licenses, consultation triggers)
Consultation record (Taiwan labor-management meeting, China union/worker representatives) where triggered
Communication plan and individual change letters
Effective-dated Darwinbox reorg transactions
processes.sla: 4-8 weeks design to implementation; longer where WARN, Mass Redundancy or Art. 41 notice periods apply

steps.label: Propose change with business case
steps.detail: Dept Head documents objectives, current and future org charts, spans and layers, roles changed, locations, timing and cost. Design uses roles, not names, until selection criteria are agreed.

steps.label: Run people impact assessment
steps.detail: List impacted roles by location and level with changes to duties, pay, reporting line and work location; flag eliminated roles, visa holders (possible H-1B amendments for worksite or duty changes), export-licensed staff whose project scope changes, and employees on protected leave.

steps.label: Identify notice and consultation triggers
steps.detail: Legal checks per country: WARN, Cal-WARN and NY/NJ mini-WARN; ON/BC group notice; Canadian constructive dismissal; Taiwan LSA Art. 10-1 transfer principles, labor-management meeting consent and Mass Redundancy thresholds; China contract-variation consent, democratic procedure and Art. 41; India retrenchment notice.

steps.label: Consultation or layoff notice needed?
steps.detail: Any statutory consultation, filing or notice period moves the timeline and the communication sequence.

steps.label: Consult employee representatives
steps.detail: China: explain Art. 41 layoffs 30 days ahead to the union or all staff, notify the union before unilateral terminations, and run democratic procedure for rule changes. Taiwan: give the Mass Redundancy plan to the authority and union or labor-management meeting labor representatives 60 days ahead and negotiate within 10 days. Minute everything; eliminations proceed under OF-03.

steps.label: Finalize design and comms plan
steps.detail: Sequence leaders, impacted individuals, teams and wider org; align with any 8-K (officer changes) and Reg FD timing; prepare country-correct change letters and consent forms where variation needs agreement.

steps.label: Announce and hold 1:1 conversations
steps.detail: Leaders deliver individual conversations before team announcements, with HRBP present for impacted roles and written change letters the same day.

steps.label: Process effective-dated changes
steps.detail: Update reporting lines, cost centers, positions and job codes in Darwinbox; the identity system adjusts approvals and access; Immigration and Trade Compliance get the change feed for affected employees.
steps.control: Approval-chain and access test before the effective date

steps.label: Org change live and audited
steps.detail: Post-implementation audit of org data, approval routing and access completed within 10 business days.

controls.control: No announcement until Legal signs the impact assessment and consultation-trigger checklist
controls.evidence: Signed checklist in document management

controls.control: Visa holders and export-licensed employees reviewed before the effective date (H-1B amendment need, license scope, I-129 Part 6 re-assessment)
controls.evidence: Immigration and Trade Compliance sign-off

controls.control: Post-implementation audit of Darwinbox org data, approval chains and access within 10 business days
controls.evidence: Audit report and access change tickets

kpis.name: Changes with legal checklist signed before announcement
kpis.why: Prevents consultation breaches and premature disclosure.

kpis.name: HRIS reorg data errors
kpis.why: Errors break approvals, payroll cost allocation and access.

kpis.name: Regretted attrition in impacted teams (6 months)
kpis.why: Signals whether the change was designed and communicated well.

considerations: Most reorgs need no consultation in the US, but the same deck applied in Shanghai or Hsinchu can trigger democratic procedure, contract-variation consent or Mass Redundancy notices; run the trigger check per country, not per project.

Moving engineers between product lines or sites can change the export analysis (new technology or ECCN) and H-1B facts (worksite or duties), so Trade Compliance and Immigration review every such reorg.
Keep design separate from selection: once names appear in design documents, they become selection evidence in discrimination and unfair-dismissal claims.
Approval chains follow reporting lines in Darwinbox, so a reorg can silently break SoD and spend approvals; test routing before the effective date.
In Canada, substantial unilateral changes to duties, reporting level or pay can be constructive dismissal; give working notice or obtain consent for significant demotions.

variations.how: Hand off to OF-03 for selection, WARN/Art. 41/Mass Redundancy notices and severance; the two timelines are merged.
Legal assesses 8-K Item 5.02 and Section 16 officer status; Comp Committee is informed.

variations.when: Cross-border function move (e.g., Shanghai to Taipei)
variations.how: Treat as a location change: MV-02/MV-03 for individuals, local exit and hiring rules at both ends, and an export-control check for the new location.

countries.us: Reorganizations need no consultation, but eliminations can trigger federal WARN (100+ employees, 60 days) and state mini-WARN (NY and NJ 90 days, NJ mandatory severance). Material changes to an H-1B worker's worksite or duties may need an amended petition, and the Sept 18, 2026 EO makes layoffs a factor in H-1B/LCA adjudication.
countries.us-ca: Cal-WARN covers mass layoffs (50+ in 30 days), relocations and terminations at a covered establishment (75+ employees), and SB 617 adds notice content on rapid-response services, workforce board contacts and CalFresh.
countries.ca: There is no consultation duty for non-union staff, but substantial unilateral changes risk constructive dismissal at common law. Eliminating 50+ roles triggers ON mass termination (Form 1 to the Director; 8-16 weeks) or BC group termination (8-16 weeks, notice to the Minister) on top of individual notice.
countries.in: Retrenching 'workers' needs 1 month's notice with reasons, notice to the government, 15 days' average pay per year of service and the re-skilling fund contribution; notify any recognized union and the Grievance Redressal Committee. Changes to service conditions of workers may require prior notice of change under the IR Code (verify).
countries.tw: Transfers must meet LSA Art. 10-1 (business need, no reduction in wages or conditions, within capability, support for distant moves), and changes to overtime or flexible-hour schemes need labor-management meeting consent. Layoffs above Mass Redundancy Protection Act thresholds need a plan filed and posted 60 days ahead with negotiation within 10 days; individual Art. 11 layoffs need the Employment Services Act Art. 33 notification 10 days before separation.
countries.cn: Changes to job, location or pay generally need written agreement to vary the labor contract, and rules affecting employees' vital interests must go through democratic procedure. Economic layoffs of 20+ employees or 10%+ need a 30-day explanation to the union or all staff and a labor bureau report (Shanghai: notify worker representatives 30 days before filing from Aug 2026), and the union must be notified before any unilateral termination.

processes.name: Contingent workforce engagement
processes.summary: Controls how the company engages non-employee labor (independent contractors, consulting SOWs, agency temps, China labor dispatch, India contract labour and EOR workers) from request through classification, screening, contracting, access and end of engagement. Good looks like every worker classified under a documented test, engaged through an approved channel, screened for export and sanctions risk, and time-limited in Darwinbox and identity systems.
processes.owner: People Ops (process and contingent register), Legal (classification), Trade Compliance (screening and technology access)
processes.trigger: A manager requests non-employee labor for a project, a temporary gap, a specialist skill or a location without an entity
outputs: Classification decision record (test applied, outcome, reviewer)
Signed contract or SOW with IP assignment, confidentiality (DTSA notice) and data terms
Restricted-party, sanctions and export-control screening result
Contingent worker record in Darwinbox with sponsor and end date
Time-bound identity and badge access grant
processes.sla: 10 business days request-to-start for agency or EOR workers; 15 for independent contractors needing classification review

steps.label: Request contingent worker
steps.detail: Manager submits a Darwinbox request: scope and deliverables, duration, location, rate, budget, whether the work is core and ongoing, who will direct it, and what systems or technology the worker needs.

steps.label: Select engagement channel
steps.detail: Choose among independent contractor, consulting-firm SOW, staffing agency, China labor dispatch, India contract labour through a licensed contractor, or EOR where there is no entity. Default for ongoing, supervised, core work is an employee req (PL-02).

steps.label: Apply worker classification test
steps.detail: Apply the local test and record it: California ABC test (AB 5), federal economic-reality test, Canadian control/integration and dependent-contractor analysis, India contract labour rules, China dispatch limits and Taiwan subordination test.

steps.label: Classification supports non-employee?
steps.detail: If the facts look like employment, the engagement is redesigned or converted rather than papered over.

steps.label: Screen worker, vendor and access need
steps.detail: Screen the individual and the vendor against the Entity List, SDN, Unverified/MEU and DOJ DSP covered-person lists, check vendor ownership ahead of the BIS Affiliates Rule's return on Nov 10, 2026, and run the TA-06 deemed-export determination if the worker needs controlled technology or source code.

steps.label: Contract and onboard worker
steps.detail: Vendor or contractor signs terms with present-tense IP assignment, confidentiality with DTSA notice and protected-rights carve-out, data terms (PIPL entrusted processing, DPDP-ready processor terms), a no-bring certification, and agency warranties on wages, social insurance and licenses.

steps.label: Provision time-bound access
steps.detail: Accounts and badges carry an end date equal to the SOW end (maximum 12 months, renewable), access matches Trade Compliance's determination, and China-resident contractors get no administrator access to global HR or identity systems (DOJ Data Security Program).

steps.label: Monitor tenure and end engagement
steps.detail: Quarterly review of tenure, integration into teams and conversion risk, plus the China dispatch ratio; at end, access is removed the same day, assets are returned and IP/confidentiality obligations are reminded in writing.
steps.control: Quarterly contingent audit (tenure, expired end dates with live access, dispatch ratio)

steps.label: Engagement closed and recorded
steps.detail: Darwinbox record closed with end reason; spend and tenure data feed PL-01.

steps.label: Route to employee hire (PL-02)
steps.detail: Manager raises an employee requisition instead; Legal advises on any conversion of an existing contractor.

controls.control: No PO, SOW or system access without a documented classification decision
controls.evidence: Classification record linked to the Darwinbox contingent record and PO

controls.control: Restricted-party and export screening completed before start; controlled-technology access only after Trade Compliance clearance
controls.evidence: Screening tool results and clearance record

controls.control: Quarterly audit of contingent tenure over 12 months, expired end dates with live access and China dispatch ratio
controls.evidence: Quarterly report with remediation tickets

controls.control: Monthly sponsor recertification of contractor accounts
controls.evidence: Access recertification records in the identity system

kpis.name: Contingent workers with documented classification
kpis.why: Classification is the core legal control.

kpis.name: Contractor accounts active past end date
kpis.why: Orphaned access is an IP and export-release risk.

kpis.name: Contingent workers with tenure over 18 months
kpis.why: Long tenure is the strongest misclassification signal.

kpis.name: China dispatch ratio
kpis.why: Statutory cap with buffer for timing.

considerations: Default to employment for ongoing, supervised, core engineering work: a 'contractor' attending design reviews for two years is an employee under nearly every test in scope, and IP ownership gets murky.

Use EOR as a bridge (typically 12-24 months) for first hires in a new country, not a permanent model; EOR still carries permanent-establishment and co-employment risk, and the EOR's local contract must carry your IP and confidentiality terms.

Contractors get the same deemed-export treatment as employees: a PRC-national contractor in the US or Canada with repository access is a release to China, so screening sits in front of access, not in the SOW.
Get IP right on paper: independent contractors own most of their work absent an express assignment, and India assignments must state duration and territory (Copyright Act s.19).
Screen vendors as well as workers: staffing agencies, EORs and recruiters in China and Taiwan can have Entity List or concealed PRC ownership.
Co-employment hygiene: managers direct deliverables, not hours, and contractors do not get employee titles, performance reviews, bonuses or equity messaging.

variations.how: Only temporary, auxiliary or substitute positions; dispatched workers at or under 10% of total workforce; equal pay for equal work; licensed dispatch agency; consider direct fixed-term contracts instead.

variations.when: India contract labour through a contractor
variations.how: Principal employer registration and contractor licensing above OSH Code thresholds (verify state rules); no contract labour in core activities; monthly check of the contractor's wage, PF and ESI compliance because the principal employer is liable for unpaid wages.

variations.when: EOR in a country without an entity
variations.how: EOR is the legal employer; the master agreement flows down IP assignment, confidentiality, data and export-screening terms; Legal checks local limits (in China, staff must be engaged through the WFOE or a licensed dispatch/HR agency).

variations.when: Former employee returning as a consultant
variations.how: Check rehire eligibility (OF-10), insider/blackout status and whether the work is genuinely independent; the California ABC test is hard to meet for the same work.

countries.us: Federal law uses the economic-reality test (DOL's Feb 26, 2026 NPRM would restore the 2021 core-factor test), while MA, NJ and IL apply ABC tests for some purposes. The 1099-NEC threshold is $2,000 for payments after Dec 31, 2025, and contractor confidentiality terms need the DTSA immunity notice.
countries.us-ca: AB 5 (Labor Code 2775 et seq.) applies the ABC test: freedom from control, work outside the usual course of the company's business, and an independently established trade; in-house chip design work fails prong B. Certain business-to-business and professional-services exemptions fall back to Borello (verify fit), and CA pay data reporting covers 100+ workers supplied through labor contractors.
countries.ca: CRA and courts weigh control, tools, chance of profit and integration; long-term 'contractors' who work like employees trigger CPP/EI assessments, and Ontario courts award reasonable notice even to dependent contractors (Keenan v. Canac, 2016 ONCA 79). Contractor IP needs an express assignment plus a moral-rights waiver.
countries.in: Contract labour rules now sit in the OSH Code 2020: principal employers register and contractors are licensed above the statutory threshold (verify state rules), core activities should not use contract labour, and the principal employer is liable for unpaid wages. Fixed-term employees must have parity with permanent staff and earn gratuity after 1 year.
countries.tw: Courts treat a 'contractor' as an employee where there is personal, economic and organizational subordination, and fixed-term renewals with gaps of 30 days or less convert to indefinite-term (LSA Art. 9). With agency dispatch, the user firm should not interview or designate specific dispatched workers in advance (LSA Art. 17-1; verify), or a direct-employment claim can arise.
countries.cn: Labor dispatch is limited to temporary, auxiliary or substitute positions, capped at 10% of the workforce, with equal pay for equal work; local staff must be employed by the WFOE or engaged through a licensed dispatch/HR agency. Individual 'consultants' doing ongoing supervised work risk a de facto labor relationship and double-wage claims for no written contract.

processes.name: Job posting & pay-range compliance
processes.summary: Makes every external and internal job posting lawful before it goes live: pay range where required, benefits summary, vacancy-status and AI-use disclosures, non-discriminatory requirements and no prohibited application questions. Covers Greenhouse postings, the careers site, job boards and agency or third-party postings in all six jurisdictions. Good looks like country and state rules encoded in Greenhouse templates so a recruiter cannot publish a non-compliant posting.
processes.owner: Talent Acquisition (process), Total Rewards (posted ranges), Legal (jurisdiction rule library)
processes.trigger: Approved requisition (PL-02) ready to post, or a material change to a live posting (range, location, remote eligibility)
outputs: Published posting with jurisdiction-required disclosures
Posted pay range record tied to the req and salary structure
Application form version free of prohibited questions
Posting archive (content, dates, channels) held for the retention period
Decision notices to interviewed applicants (Ontario)
processes.sla: Posting live within 2 business days of req approval

steps.label: Draft posting from approved req
steps.detail: Recruiter uses the Greenhouse template selected by work location and remote eligibility; the job description comes from the job code. No 'US citizens only' without a legal or contract basis, no 'Canadian experience' requirement, and no age, gender or marital criteria.

steps.label: Confirm posted pay range
steps.detail: Posted range is the good-faith estimate of base pay the company expects to pay at hire for that location, not the full structure min-max. Ontario spread is capped at C$50,000; add a benefits and incentive summary where required (e.g., CT, WA).

steps.label: Add jurisdiction disclosures
steps.detail: Add AI-use statement (Ontario; NYC LL144 and Illinois notices), Ontario vacancy-exists statement, CCPA notice-at-collection link, EEO statement, Taiwan salary range for roles under NT$40,000/month, and trigger India National Career Service vacancy reporting.

steps.label: Compliance check passed?
steps.detail: Standard templates pass an automated checklist; Legal reviews only new jurisdictions or non-standard content.

steps.label: Publish and syndicate posting
steps.detail: Publish to careers site, boards and approved agencies with the same range (third-party postings count in California); remote postings list eligible states or provinces.

steps.label: Archive posting and application form
steps.detail: Snapshot the posting, application form, dates and channels to document management; retain at least 3 years (Ontario), 4 years (California) and 1 year (US federal).

steps.label: Notify interviewed applicants
steps.detail: Send decision status to every interviewed applicant within 45 days of their last interview (Ontario requirement; company standard elsewhere).

steps.label: Posting closed; records retained
steps.detail: Posting is closed in Greenhouse when the req fills or cancels; records stay under retention.

raci.activity: Maintain jurisdiction rule library and templates

controls.control: Greenhouse blocks publishing without a range for jobs located in or remote-eligible for range jurisdictions
controls.evidence: Greenhouse configuration and publish audit log

controls.control: Monthly sample of live postings against the rule library (range, Ontario spread, AI and vacancy statements, prohibited requirements)
controls.evidence: Audit worksheet with remediation

controls.control: Application forms carry no salary-history, pre-offer criminal-history or protected-ground questions; changes need Legal approval
controls.evidence: Form version history with approvals

controls.control: Quarterly comparison of hires' starting base pay with posted ranges
controls.evidence: Range adherence report

kpis.name: Postings compliant on audit
kpis.why: Penalties run per posting (CA $100-$10,000 per violation).

kpis.name: Hires with base pay inside posted range
kpis.why: Tests whether posted ranges are genuine good-faith estimates.

kpis.name: Ontario interviewees notified within 45 days
kpis.why: Statutory duty and a candidate-experience signal.

considerations: Post the range you will actually pay: SB 642 defines the pay scale as the good-faith estimate of what you reasonably expect to pay at hire, so posting a full structure range (e.g., $120k-$260k) is itself a risk.

Treat 'Remote - US' as every state: CO, WA, NY, IL, MN, MD, NJ, VT, MA and the 2026 additions VA, ME and CT can reach remote roles, so one good-faith range plus a benefits summary on every US posting is simpler than carve-outs.
AI disclosure is now a posting requirement in Ontario and a notice requirement in NYC and Illinois; inventory which Greenhouse add-ons score or rank applicants before writing the sentence.

For export-sensitive roles say 'this role requires access to export-controlled technology; employment may be contingent on export authorization', not 'US persons only', which invites 8 U.S.C. 1324b claims.
Agencies and job boards republish your posts: contract for their compliance and give them only the approved range.

variations.how: Ontario internal-only postings are outside the ESA posting rules, but Virginia requires ranges in internal postings; use the same template everywhere.
Ontario postings must say whether a vacancy currently exists, so state 'no current vacancy'; California and other range rules still apply.

variations.when: Executive search with no public posting
variations.how: Posting rules are not triggered, but California applicants can request the pay scale, so keep the range on the req.

countries.us: Ranges are required in covered postings in CO, WA, NY, HI, DC, MD, IL, MN, NJ, VT, MA and Cleveland, joined by VA (Jul 1, 2026), ME (Jul 29, 2026) and CT (Oct 1, 2026, with a benefits description), with DE following on Sept 26, 2027. Remove salary-history questions (20+ states and cities) and give NYC LL144 notice 10 business days before using an automated employment decision tool.
countries.us-ca: Employers with 15+ employees must include the pay scale in every posting for a role that may be filled in California, including remote and third-party postings (LC 432.3; SB 1162, SB 642), with penalties of $100-$10,000 per violation. A driver's license requirement is allowed only where driving is reasonably expected and alternatives are not comparable (SB 1100).
countries.ca: Ontario (25+ employees, from Jan 1, 2026): public postings need pay or a range with a spread of no more than C$50,000 (roles over C$200,000 exempt), a vacancy-status statement and disclosure of AI used to screen, assess or select, with no 'Canadian experience' requirement, 3-year record retention and notice to interviewees within 45 days. BC public postings must show expected pay or a range (since Nov 1, 2023) and cannot ask about pay history.
countries.in: There is no pay-range rule, but vacancies must be reported to the National Career Service before filling under the Social Security Code rules. Keep wording gender-neutral (including transgender) and avoid criteria on caste, religion, marital or pregnancy status.
countries.tw: Postings for roles with regular pay under NT$40,000/month must show a salary range (Employment Services Act Art. 5). Discriminatory criteria such as marital status, pregnancy plans, horoscope, blood type or age risk fines of NT$300,000-1,500,000.
countries.cn: Remove gender, marital or childbearing status, ethnicity, religion and health-status criteria and hard age caps from ads (Employment Promotion Law; Women's Rights Law 2022 Art. 43). Post local roles in Chinese and link the PIPL candidate privacy notice.

processes.name: Sourcing, agencies & referrals
processes.summary: Runs candidate sourcing through direct sourcing, employee referrals, university channels and approved agencies under consistent, lawful and auditable rules. Covers agency selection and terms, referral bonus administration, antitrust and clean-sourcing boundaries, and anti-corruption review of sensitive referrals. Good looks like every candidate entering Greenhouse with a tracked source and privacy notice, agencies working under signed terms after ownership screening, and referral bonuses paid correctly through payroll.
processes.owner: Talent Acquisition (process), Ethics & Compliance (sensitive referrals), Legal (agency terms, antitrust), Payroll (referral bonuses)
processes.trigger: Open requisition needing a sourcing plan, or an inbound referral or agency submission
outputs: Sourcing plan per req (channels, target profiles, outreach open to all)
Approved agency list with signed terms and screening results
Candidate source and privacy-notice records in Greenhouse
Referral bonus eligibility decisions and payroll instructions
Compliance review record for official- or customer-connected referrals
processes.sla: Sourcing plan within 3 business days of req open; referrals acknowledged within 5 business days

steps.label: Build sourcing plan with manager
steps.detail: Agree channels, target profiles and target companies with the manager; outreach is broad and open to all. Recruiters never solicit competitors' confidential information (org charts, roadmaps, comp files) from candidates.

steps.label: Submit referral in Greenhouse
steps.detail: Employees refer through the Greenhouse referral portal, not email, and disclose their relationship to the candidate; relatives are flagged for TA-10 review.

steps.label: Official or customer connection?
steps.detail: Referrals from, or candidates related to, government officials, SOE employees, customers or suppliers need review before any offer.

steps.label: Review sensitive referral
steps.detail: Confirm the candidate goes through the standard merit process with no commitments or link to business; record the review and keep it at least 5 years.

steps.label: Agency submits under signed terms
steps.detail: Only approved agencies submit, under terms covering fee, guarantee period, candidate ownership, duplicate-submission rules, compliance with posting, salary-history and privacy laws, and candidate consent to submission. Agencies are pre-screened for restricted-party status and ownership.

steps.label: Log source, send notice, screen
steps.detail: Every candidate gets a source tag and the jurisdictional privacy notice at first contact (TA-11); knockout questions stay minimal and job-related.

steps.label: Pay referral bonus when eligible
steps.detail: After the referred hire completes the eligibility period, the bonus is paid through payroll as supplemental wages; hiring managers, recruiters and interviewers on the req are ineligible.

steps.label: Candidate in process; source tracked
steps.detail: Candidate proceeds to TA-03 with source, consent and review records attached.

controls.control: Agencies engaged only under signed terms after restricted-party and ownership screening
controls.evidence: Approved agency list, screening results and signed terms

controls.control: Referrals connected to government officials, SOEs or customers reviewed by Compliance before offer
controls.evidence: Greenhouse flag and Compliance review record retained 5 years

controls.control: Quarterly referral bonus audit (eligibility, ineligible referrers, payroll treatment)
controls.evidence: Audit report with corrections

kpis.name: Referral share of engineering hires
kpis.why: Referrals are the cheapest, best-retained source in a tight chip market.

kpis.name: Agency share of hires
kpis.why: Agency fees are a major controllable cost.

kpis.name: Candidates with source and notice recorded
kpis.why: Needed for adverse-impact analysis and privacy compliance.

considerations: Never agree with other chip companies, customers, foundry or JV partners not to hire each other's staff or to align pay; Canada has criminalized no-poach and wage-fixing agreements since June 23, 2023, and US antitrust enforcers treat naked no-poach deals as violations. Any non-solicit must be tied to a legitimate transaction and approved by Legal.
Target-company sourcing is lawful; target-information sourcing is not. Train recruiters to stop candidates who start describing a current employer's confidential designs or plans.
Diverse outreach must stay open to all: no race- or sex-restricted slates or demographic-linked referral bonuses (DOJ's $17M IBM False Claims Act settlement targeted diverse-slate rules).

In Taiwan, MJIB has run 100+ investigations into covert PRC-linked recruiting; vet headhunters for concealed PRC ownership and never use them to approach staff on national core key technology projects.
Referral bonuses are wages: pay them through payroll with the right withholding and write the program terms precisely so eligibility disputes at exit do not become wage claims.

variations.when: Customer or government official refers a candidate
variations.how: Compliance review, documented merit process, no special treatment; customer-requested internships are declined (open-application only).

variations.when: Sourcing from a direct competitor or Entity List company
variations.how: Allowed, but the TA-10 clean-hire protocol applies before offer (prior agreements review, no-bring certification, enhanced onboarding); never a proxy for nationality.
Handled under TA-09; the search contract's off-limits and fee terms are reviewed by Legal.

countries.us: Referral bonuses are supplemental wages subject to withholding and must not be demographically targeted; salary-history bans in 20+ states and cities apply to agencies acting for you. Agencies posting for CO, WA, NY and other range states must carry your approved range.
countries.us-ca: Agencies and background vendors cannot ask salary history on your behalf (LC 432.3), and third-party postings for California-eligible roles need the pay scale. The CCPA notice at collection must cover data received from agencies and sourcing tools.
countries.ca: The Competition Act makes no-poach and wage-fixing agreements between employers a criminal offence (since June 23, 2023), and private access to the Competition Tribunal opened in June 2025. BC applicants cannot be asked about pay history, including by agencies.
countries.in: Counter-offers and offer reneging are common, so track agency guarantee and replacement terms, and expect notice-period buy-outs as market practice. Put agencies under written processing terms ahead of DPDP duties starting 13 May 2027.
countries.tw: Vet agencies for concealed PRC ownership; the Cross-Strait Act restricts PRC-linked recruiting in Taiwan and MJIB questioned 114 people at 17 firms in Jul-Aug 2026. Use licensed private employment service agencies (verify licensing for each vendor).
countries.cn: Sign entrusted-processing agreements with recruiters and screening vendors (PIPL Art. 21) and obtain candidate consent before reference calls. Referral payments to non-employees or customer staff raise commercial bribery risk under the Anti-Unfair Competition Law.

processes.name: Structured interview & selection
processes.summary: Defines how candidates are assessed and chosen: job-related competencies agreed up front, trained interviewers, structured questions with anchored Greenhouse scorecards submitted independently before debrief, a documented hiring decision, and governance of any AI or automated screening tool. Covers every role from intern to VP in all six jurisdictions. Good looks like fast, consistent, evidence-based decisions that stand up to disparate-impact scrutiny and never rely on a prohibited question.
processes.owner: Talent Acquisition (process), Hiring Manager (decision), Legal (AI tool governance), HR Analytics (adverse-impact monitoring)
processes.trigger: Requisition opened in Greenhouse (PL-02/TA-01) and intake meeting scheduled
outputs: Interview plan and T-SCORECARD in Greenhouse (competencies, anchors, question bank)
Independent interviewer scorecards submitted before debrief
Debrief or hiring-committee decision record with competency-based rationale
AI tool register entry, bias audit or anti-bias testing evidence, and candidate notices
Stage-by-stage adverse-impact reports
Candidate dispositions with reason codes and notices
processes.sla: Intake to hiring decision <=30 days; scorecards within 24 hours; debrief within 2 business days of the final interview

steps.label: Hold intake and define competencies
steps.detail: Recruiter and manager agree 4-6 job-related competencies from the job code (e.g., RTL design, UVM verification, analog layout, customer debugging), must-haves vs nice-to-haves, level calibration and the interview loop. 'Culture fit' is not a criterion.

steps.label: Approve plan and T-SCORECARD
steps.detail: Scorecard has behavioral or technical anchors on a 1-4 scale, a question bank per competency and assigned interviewers. Technical exercises must be job-related, time-boxed and identical for all candidates at the level.

steps.label: AI or automated tool in the loop?
steps.detail: Any tool that scores, ranks, filters or recommends candidates (resume match scores, auto-graded coding tests, video analysis, chatbots that screen) counts.

steps.label: Clear AI tool and send notices
steps.detail: Tool must be on the AI register (DS-06) with vendor terms: NYC LL144 annual bias audit, public summary and notice 10 business days before use; Illinois notice; California CRD ADS anti-bias testing, accommodation route and 4-year data retention; Ontario posting disclosure. Every automated rejection gets human review.
steps.control: No AI screening without register entry, Legal approval and required notices

steps.label: Screen applicants on must-haves
steps.detail: Screen resumes against documented must-haves; phone screens use standard questions. Ask pay expectations, never salary history; no criminal-history questions before a conditional offer; the only status questions are the approved work-authorization and sponsorship questions.

steps.label: Schedule loop and brief panel
steps.detail: Schedule only interviewers with current training; offer accommodations (ADA, FEHA, AODA, RPwD). Onsite visits for export-flagged roles use public or sanitized material: no lab tours or proprietary code walk-throughs before Trade Compliance clearance.
steps.control: Only trained interviewers can be scheduled

steps.label: Complete interviews and exercises
steps.detail: Candidate completes the structured loop and any exercise under the same conditions as other candidates; accommodation requests are handled without recording disability on the scorecard.

steps.label: Interviewers submit scorecards in 24h
steps.detail: Each interviewer rates only assigned competencies with evidence; Greenhouse hides others' feedback until one's own scorecard is submitted. Notes never reference protected characteristics.

steps.label: Run debrief or hiring committee
steps.detail: Start from written scorecards and discuss evidence per competency, junior interviewers first; hiring committee for senior levels and campus calibration. Decision and rationale are recorded in Greenhouse.

steps.label: Hire decision?
steps.detail: Manager decides on the evidence; a hiring committee decides for senior levels.

steps.label: Hand off to offer approval
steps.detail: Pass level recommendation, competency evidence and comp inputs to TA-04; references and checks follow TA-05 after the conditional offer.

steps.label: Disposition and notify candidates
steps.detail: Close every other candidate with a reason code and timely notice (Ontario: interviewed applicants within 45 days); records retained per TA-11.

steps.label: Monitor adverse impact by stage
steps.detail: Quarterly pass-through rates by stage and by tool for sex, race/ethnicity (US voluntary self-ID) and age band where lawful, using the four-fifths rule plus statistical tests; results go to Legal under privilege with action items.

steps.label: Selection documented and closed
steps.detail: Greenhouse holds the plan, scorecards, decision rationale, notices and dispositions for the req.

raci.activity: AI/automated tool approval, audits and notices
Scheduling, accommodations and onsite access rules

controls.control: Only interviewers with interviewer training completed in the last 12 months can be scheduled (Greenhouse permission tied to LMS completion)
controls.evidence: LMS completion report and Greenhouse interviewer list

controls.control: Scorecards are submitted independently before debrief; peer feedback is hidden until one's own scorecard is in
controls.evidence: Greenhouse configuration and submission timestamps

controls.control: No AI or automated screening tool is used without register entry, Legal approval, bias audit or anti-bias testing and required notices
controls.evidence: AI tool register, LL144 audit summary, notice logs, CA ADS data retained 4 years

controls.control: Quarterly adverse-impact analysis by stage and by tool
controls.evidence: Privileged analysis memo and action log

controls.control: An offer cannot be created until a hire decision with competency rationale is recorded
controls.evidence: Greenhouse decision field and offer-workflow gate

controls.control: Quarterly audit of screening questions and knockout rules (salary history, pre-offer criminal history, protected grounds, citizenship)
controls.evidence: ATS question audit worksheet

kpis.name: Scorecards submitted within 24 hours
kpis.why: Late scorecards are anchored by debrief chatter.

kpis.name: Final interview to decision
kpis.why: Strong engineers hold multiple offers.

kpis.name: Adverse-impact ratio at each stage
kpis.why: Four-fifths rule is the standard early-warning test.

kpis.name: Offer acceptance rate (engineering)
kpis.why: Measures candidate experience and calibration.

kpis.name: 12-month retention of hires
kpis.why: Tests whether selection predicts success.

kpis.name: Interviewer training currency
kpis.why: Structured interviewing only works with trained panels.

considerations: Structure beats charisma: the same competencies, questions and anchors for every candidate at a level is both the best predictor and the best legal defense. Unstructured 'chat' rounds with senior engineers are where bias creeps in.
Independence before debrief: require scorecards before the debrief and hear the most junior interviewer first to avoid anchoring on the most senior voice.
Exercises should mirror the job (debug a failing testbench, review a timing report) with a fixed time box and rubric; unpaid multi-day take-homes deter strong candidates who are serving notice.

Any tool that scores, ranks or filters applicants is an ADS under California CRD rules and may be an AEDT under NYC LL144, and the company is liable for vendor tools acting as its agent. Keep a register and test for bias before and after deployment.
Monitor adverse impact by stage and by tool: a clean overall hire rate can hide a biased resume screen.

Onsite interviews in labs or with code walk-throughs can be a 'release' of controlled technology to a foreign-person candidate; keep interview content at published level unless Trade Compliance clears the candidate.
Hiring committees for senior levels reduce single-manager bias and calibrate leveling across San Jose, Toronto, Vancouver, Bengaluru, Hsinchu and Shanghai.
Dispositions matter: Ontario requires notice to interviewed applicants within 45 days, and fast, respectful rejections protect the brand in a small chip-talent market.

variations.how: Standard assessment and hiring committee calibrate across schools; TA-08 sets the calendar; AI-screening notices apply to high-volume funnels.
Search firm, CEO and board interviews, structured leadership competencies and referencing under TA-09; CHRO sits on the hiring committee.
Same scorecard and panel; performance data used only as POL-43 allows; HRBP delivers decisions personally.
Adjust format (extra time, alternative exercise, remote interview) under ADA, FEHA, AODA or RPwD; do not record disability on the scorecard.
Interview content uses public or sanitized material; no lab tours or proprietary code demos until Trade Compliance clears the candidate (TA-06).

variations.when: High-volume hiring with AI screening in NYC, Illinois or California
variations.how: Bias audit (NYC) and notices issued before use, human review of all automated rejections, 4-year ADS record retention in California.

countries.us: Title VII disparate-impact liability applies regardless of EO 14281, and Ames v. Ohio (2025) removed extra hurdles for majority-group plaintiffs, so selection must be non-preferential for everyone. NYC LL144 requires an annual independent bias audit, a public summary and notice 10 business days before using an AEDT; Illinois HB 3773 (from Jan 1, 2026) requires notice of AI use and bars discriminatory effect, and Colorado SB 26-189 adds notice and explanation duties from Jan 1, 2027. No disability inquiries or medical exams before a conditional offer (ADA).
countries.us-ca: CRD automated-decision system regulations (effective Oct 1, 2025) make the employer liable for discriminatory ADS, including vendors acting as agents; document anti-bias testing, offer accommodations and keep ADS inputs and outputs for 4 years. CCPA ADMT pre-use notice and opt-out or appeal rights start Jan 1, 2027. No criminal-history questions before a conditional offer and no questions about past cannabis use (Gov Code 12952, 12954).
countries.ca: Do not ask about protected grounds (in Ontario including citizenship and record of offences) and offer accommodation during recruitment (AODA IASR s.22-23). Ontario employers with 25+ employees must disclose AI used in screening in postings and tell interviewed applicants the outcome within 45 days, keeping postings, forms and notices for 3 years.
countries.in: India has no general private-sector anti-discrimination statute, but gender (including transgender) neutrality, disability accommodation and no HIV-status questions are required (Code on Wages s.3; RPwD Act; Transgender Persons Act; HIV/AIDS Act). Avoid questions on caste, religion, marital or pregnancy status, and give notice for assessment data ahead of DPDP duties from 13 May 2027.
countries.tw: Interview questions and forms must not cover marital status, pregnancy plans, horoscope, blood type or age (Employment Services Act Art. 5; fines NT$300,000-1,500,000), and passports or ID cards must never be held. Tell candidates from TSMC, MediaTek or UMC not to disclose prior-employer technical details during interviews.
countries.cn: Do not ask women about marriage or pregnancy plans or screen on health status, ethnicity or religion (Employment Promotion Law; Women's Rights Law Art. 43); pre-employment medicals exclude hepatitis B markers and pregnancy tests. Written, measurable hiring criteria documented at selection become the probation criteria needed for any Art. 39(1) probation dismissal.

processes.name: Offer approval & extension
processes.summary: Turns a hire decision into an approved, compliant offer: base within band, equity sized to guidelines, sign-on and relocation within policy and local law, approvals per matrix, and a country-correct offer letter with contingencies and an IP/confidentiality agreement. Covers all employee offers in all six jurisdictions, including contractor and intern conversions. Good looks like offers approved within 2 business days, no out-of-band offer without a documented exception, and letters that are enforceable where the employee works.
processes.owner: Talent Acquisition (process), Total Rewards (bands and equity guidelines), Legal (offer and contract templates)
outputs: Approved T-OFFER-APPROVAL (band position, equity, sign-on, approvals)
Country-specific offer letter and, where needed, full employment contract
IP/confidentiality (PIIA) agreement with required notices
Contingency tracker (background, export, work authorization, references)
New-hire equity grant request for the next scheduled grant date
Signed acceptance and Darwinbox pre-hire record
processes.sla: Offer approved within 2 business days of decision; written offer within 1 business day of verbal

steps.label: Gather comp inputs and expectations
steps.detail: Collect pay expectations, competing offers the candidate chooses to share, notice period, location, visa status and relocation needs. Never ask or rely on salary history (banned in CA, BC and 20+ US states and cities; company-wide ban recommended).

steps.label: Build offer in T-OFFER-APPROVAL
steps.detail: Level from TA-03; base from the location band with target compa-ratio; target bonus by level; new-hire equity from the grant guideline expressed as value and converted by the plan's method; sign-on and relocation within policy; target start date.

steps.label: Check band, equity and pay equity
steps.detail: Validate base against range and against incumbents in the same job code and location, equity against guideline, sign-on structure against local law (AB 692 in California; reasonable liquidated damages in India), CA exempt floor and India 50% wages structure.

steps.label: Within guidelines?
steps.detail: In-guideline offers go straight to manager approval.

steps.label: Approve exception per matrix
steps.detail: Above band maximum or above equity guideline needs Dept Head plus Head of Total Rewards; above a set multiple of guideline needs CHRO; officer and NEO packages go to the Comp Committee via TA-09. Rationale is recorded on the form.
steps.control: Documented exception approval for any out-of-guideline element

steps.label: Approve final offer package
steps.detail: Hiring manager (and Dept Head for senior levels) approves in the Greenhouse workflow; the recruiter cannot be an approver.
steps.control: Offer letter cannot generate until all approvals are complete

steps.label: Generate country-correct letter
steps.detail: Greenhouse merges approved terms into the Legal-owned template for the country or state; clauses are locked and any deviation goes to Legal. Templates include contingencies, PIIA with DTSA immunity notice and protected-rights carve-out, and local mandatory content.

steps.label: Extend verbal then written offer
steps.detail: Verbal offer covers key terms; the written offer follows the same day by e-signature with a reasonable expiry (e.g., 5 business days). Equity is described as a recommendation subject to Comp Committee or delegate approval on a scheduled grant date.

steps.label: Review, negotiate and sign
steps.detail: Candidate signs the offer and PIIA (in Canada the full contract, before the start date). Material changes loop back through Total Rewards.

steps.label: Offer accepted?
steps.detail: Record outcome and reasons in Greenhouse.

steps.label: Track contingencies to clearance
steps.detail: Track background (TA-05), export clearance (TA-06), work authorization (TA-07) and references; the Darwinbox start date is gated until each clears or a documented exception exists.

steps.label: Submit new-hire equity grant
steps.detail: Submit the grant request in the equity platform for the first scheduled grant date after start, under Comp Committee delegated authority; no officer option grants in the Item 402(x) window; store any sign-on agreement with the offer.

steps.label: Pre-hire created; hand to ON-01
steps.detail: Accepted offer, contract and contingency status flow into preboarding (ON-01) and the hire transaction (ON-03).

steps.label: Offer declined; reasons logged
steps.detail: Decline reason captured (comp, counteroffer, location, role) for TA and Total Rewards analytics; the req returns to the pipeline.

raci.activity: Offer letter and contract templates, deviations

controls.control: Offer cannot be generated in Greenhouse until T-OFFER-APPROVAL is fully approved per matrix
controls.evidence: Greenhouse approval chain export

controls.control: Base outside band or equity above guideline requires documented exception approval
controls.evidence: Exception log with rationale and approvers

controls.control: Only Legal-approved country templates with locked clauses; deviations need Legal approval
controls.evidence: Template library version log and deviation approvals

controls.control: New-hire equity is granted only by the Comp Committee or its delegate on scheduled grant dates
controls.evidence: Committee or delegate approvals and grant calendar
