controls.control: Monthly reconciliation of accepted offers to Darwinbox pre-hires and equity grant requests
controls.evidence: Reconciliation report with exceptions cleared

controls.control: Salary-history fields removed from Greenhouse forms and offer templates
controls.evidence: ATS configuration audit

controls.control: Quarterly pay-equity check of new-hire offers against incumbents in the same job code and location
controls.evidence: Pay-equity dashboard and remediation list (CO-05/CO-06)

kpis.name: Offer approval cycle time
kpis.why: Speed wins candidates holding multiple offers.

kpis.name: Offer acceptance rate
kpis.why: Primary signal that offers are competitive and well-run.

kpis.name: Out-of-guideline offers
kpis.why: Tests guideline realism and control discipline.

kpis.name: Offer letter defects
kpis.why: Wrong templates create unenforceable terms and penalties.

kpis.name: New-hire vs incumbent compa-ratio gap
kpis.target: Within +/-5 points in same job code and location
kpis.why: New-hire offers are the main source of pay compression.

considerations: Anchor on expectations, not history: removing salary-history questions globally is simpler than state-by-state rules and protects the equal-pay defense (in California, voluntarily disclosed history cannot justify a pay gap).
Check every offer against incumbents in the same job code and location before approval, and budget off-cycle fixes (CO-05) when a market offer leapfrogs the team.
Express equity as a value converted by a defined method and grant on scheduled dates; never promise a unit count before approval, and keep officer option grants out of the Item 402(x) window.

AB 692 changes sign-on design in California: for agreements on or after Jan 1, 2026, repayment of training, relocation or other debts at exit is barred, with narrow exceptions such as discretionary upfront bonuses under a standalone agreement. Prefer forward-vesting cash or RSUs and watch AB 1697 (Governor action by Sept 30, 2026), which would move the start to Jan 1, 2027 and extend the exception to retention bonuses.

Canada: the contract must be signed before the start date, with an ESA-compliant termination clause and equity terms that exclude the common-law notice period (Matthews); a contract signed on Day 10 needs fresh consideration.
Make contingencies explicit and time-bound in the letter (background, export authorization, work authorization, references, signed PIIA) and gate the Darwinbox start date on them.
India: expect 60-90 day notice periods and reneging; use joining bonuses with pro-rated clawbacks (enforceable only as reasonable liquidated damages) and keep candidates engaged during notice.
Taiwan and China candidates compare total cash (profit sharing, multi-month bonuses) with TSMC, MediaTek or domestic chip firms, so show annualized total value including RSUs, not just base.

The PIIA must carry the DTSA immunity notice, SEC Rule 21F-17 protected-rights language, state invention carve-out notices (CA LC 2870 and others) and local formalities (India s.19 duration and territory; Taiwan employer named as author).

variations.how: Route to TA-09: Comp Committee approval, 8-K Item 5.02 assessment, and a Nasdaq 5635(c)(4) inducement grant if made outside the plan.
Immigration (TA-07) confirms route and cost before the offer; the letter conditions start on work authorization; H-1B offers meet the required wage level.

variations.when: Counteroffer from current employer or a competitor
variations.how: Recruiter returns to Total Rewards; improvements above guideline need exception approval and must respect internal-equity guardrails.
Handled under MV-03 with a new local contract; the letter addresses ending the old contract, service recognition and any severance continuity (China, Taiwan).
Legal review first: in China and Taiwan an accepted offer is binding and may carry damages, and in Canada notice damages can apply; rely on a documented failed contingency.
TA-10 clean-hire certification and prior-agreement review before offer; California voids out-of-state non-competes but trade-secret risk remains.
Standard cohort packages from TA-08 with reasonable response deadlines.

countries.us: Offer letters should state at-will status and exempt or non-exempt classification and list contingencies (I-9, background check, PIIA with DTSA notice). Do not use non-competes for employees in MN, ND, OK, WY, CA or (from Jun 30, 2027) WA, and check income thresholds elsewhere (CO, IL, OR, VA, DC, ME). Salary-history bans in 20+ states and cities, including VA from Jul 2026, apply to offer negotiations.
countries.us-ca: Use California templates: no non-compete (B&P 16600), no non-CA law or forum unless the employee is individually represented by counsel (LC 925), no stay-or-pay or repayment terms for agreements entered on or after Jan 1, 2026 (AB 692; minimum $5,000 damages per worker), and the LC 2870 invention carve-out notice. Do not ask about or rely on salary history (LC 432.3); exempt offers must meet $70,304 (2026) or $72,384 (2027), and non-exempt hires get an LC 2810.5 wage notice.
countries.ca: Send a Canadian contract with an ESA-compliant termination clause, IP assignment and moral-rights waiver, and equity forfeiture language that excludes the common-law notice period, signed before the start date; Ontario non-competes are void below the C-suite (ESA s.67.2). Ontario employers with 25+ employees must give the written new-hire information statement before Day 1, and BC offers cannot be based on pay history.
countries.in: Issue the offer letter, then the statutory appointment letter at joining (OSH Code s.6(1)(f)) showing designation, worker or non-worker category, wages structured so statutory 'wages' are at least 50%, PF/ESI/gratuity and notice terms. Stamp the employment agreement (Karnataka e-stamp) and draft the IP assignment as perpetual and worldwide (Copyright Act s.19); post-employment non-competes are void (Contract Act s.27).
countries.tw: Put the Enforcement Rules Art. 7 terms in writing (duties, location with a reasonable transfer clause, hours and overtime approval, wage components, bonus, leave, termination) with a Traditional Chinese version. Any post-employment non-compete must meet LSA Art. 9-1 (maximum 2 years, compensation of at least 50% of average monthly wage, in writing), and IP clauses should name the employer as author (Copyright Act Art. 11) and address service-invention remuneration.
countries.cn: An accepted offer is a binding pre-contract commitment; sign the bilingual labor contract on or before Day 1 and never later than one month, or double wages apply (LCL Arts. 10, 82). Probation must match the contract term (maximum 1, 2 or 6 months) at 80%+ of wage, and non-competes are only for senior management and senior technical staff, with monthly post-exit compensation of at least 30% of prior average pay (MOHRSS 2025 Guidelines).

processes.name: Background & reference checks
processes.summary: Runs lawful, consistent and job-related pre-employment screening after a conditional offer: disclosures and consent, vendor checks (identity, education, employment, criminal where permitted, credit only for listed roles), structured references, and a fair adverse-action process. Scope is all new hires, rehires and contractor conversions in six jurisdictions. Good looks like checks cleared in about a week, local consent rules followed, and no decision made on a report without the required notices.
processes.owner: Talent Acquisition Operations (process), Legal (screening matrix and adverse decisions), Background-check vendor (execution)
outputs: Signed disclosure and consent forms per jurisdiction
Vendor background report and reference summaries
Individualized assessment and pre-adverse/adverse notices where applicable
Clearance decision recorded in Greenhouse and Darwinbox
Screening records stored separately from the personnel file
processes.sla: Initiate within 1 business day of acceptance; clear within 7 business days (India education and employment verification 10-15)

steps.label: Initiate checks per screening matrix
steps.detail: Package is set by country and role from Legal's matrix (e.g., credit only for listed roles, enhanced references for trade-secret-heavy roles), and only after the conditional offer.

steps.label: Sign disclosures and consents
steps.detail: US FCRA standalone disclosure and authorization plus state forms (CA ICRAA); Canada consent and Ontario consumer-reporting notice; India BGV consent with voluntary, masked Aadhaar; Taiwan PDPA notice and written consent for criminal or health data; China PIPL consent.

steps.label: Run checks and references
steps.detail: Identity, education, employment (in China, the prior employer's termination certificate), criminal where lawful, and structured references with consent; the vendor works under a processing agreement.

steps.label: Report clear?
steps.detail: Any criminal record, discrepancy or unverifiable item goes to assessment; nothing is decided automatically.

steps.label: Complete individualized assessment
steps.detail: Assess nature and gravity, time elapsed and relevance to the job (written in California); investigate credential discrepancies; never consider arrests without conviction or sealed or diverted records.

steps.label: Send pre-adverse notice and wait
steps.detail: Send the pre-adverse notice with a copy of the report and Summary of Rights, then wait at least 5 business days (California adds 5 more if the candidate disputes) and consider any evidence of rehabilitation or error.

steps.label: Proceed with hire?
steps.detail: Decision documented with reasons.

steps.label: Record clearance; release start
steps.detail: Clearance recorded in Greenhouse and Darwinbox; the start date is released if other contingencies are met.

steps.label: Cleared to start
steps.detail: Screening file closed and stored separately from the personnel file.

steps.label: Final notice sent; offer withdrawn
steps.detail: Final adverse action notice with the vendor's contact details and dispute rights (in California, the right to file with CRD); offer withdrawn and records retained.

raci.activity: Screening matrix by country and role

controls.control: No check starts before the conditional offer or without jurisdiction-specific consent
controls.evidence: E-signature consent timestamps compared with offer acceptance

controls.control: No adverse decision without individualized assessment, pre-adverse notice and waiting period
controls.evidence: Notice copies and dates in the case file

controls.control: Annual vendor audit (FCRA compliance, data location, PIPL/DPDP processing terms, retention)
controls.evidence: Vendor audit report

kpis.name: Median time to clear
kpis.why: Screening should not delay start dates.

kpis.name: Adverse actions with complete notice trail
kpis.why: FCRA and Fair Chance Act class actions turn on notice defects.

kpis.name: Start dates delayed by screening
kpis.why: Shows initiation and vendor performance.

considerations: Check what the role needs, not what the vendor sells: one global 'full package' breaks California credit limits, China's lack of private criminal checks and Taiwan's sensitive-data rules.
Make post-conditional-offer criminal checks with individualized assessment the global default; it satisfies California, NYC, Illinois, Washington and others and is fair everywhere.

Degree and employment verification catch most fraud in engineering hiring; in India verify directly with institutions and prior employers, and never keep original certificates (now banned in Karnataka).
References use structured questions tied to TA-03 competencies and only with consent; never call a current employer without permission.
Store screening results outside the personnel file and purge them on the TA-11 schedule.

variations.when: Role with trade-secret, finance or cash access
variations.how: Credit check only where lawful (California LC 1024.5 listed roles include access to trade secrets or $10,000+ cash); enhanced references elsewhere.
Refresh identity and criminal checks only and confirm rehire eligibility (OF-10, TA-10).
Government investigation replaces or adds to vendor checks; California cannabis protections do not apply to clearance roles.
Decision pauses while the vendor reinvestigates; California allows 5 more business days.

countries.us: FCRA requires a standalone disclosure and written authorization, a pre-adverse action notice with the report and Summary of Rights, a waiting period (commonly 5 business days) and a final adverse action notice (15 U.S.C. 1681b(b), 1681m). Fair-chance laws in NYC, Illinois, Washington and elsewhere delay criminal questions until after a conditional offer and require individualized assessment.
countries.us-ca: Under the Fair Chance Act (Gov Code 12952) there are no criminal checks before a conditional offer, then a written individualized assessment, a preliminary notice with 5 business days to respond (plus 5 if disputing) and a final notice citing the right to file with CRD. Give separate ICRAA and FCRA disclosures; credit checks only for listed roles (LC 1024.5).
countries.ca: Criminal and credit checks need a legitimate job requirement and consent; Ontario requires notice under the Consumer Reporting Act and protects 'record of offences' as a ground. BC PIPA allows collection reasonable for the employment relationship, with notice.
countries.in: Use written BGV consent covering education, employment, address and criminal checks through court records or police verification; Aadhaar must be voluntary and masked. DPDP s.7(i) may cover recruitment, but keep consent until case law settles, and Karnataka bans holding original certificates.
countries.tw: Give a PDPA notice at collection; criminal records and health data are sensitive and need written consent or a statutory basis. Keep checks job-related and proportionate, and handle the employer-paid pre-employment medical exam results as sensitive data.
countries.cn: Private employers cannot obtain official criminal-record checks; get PIPL consent for background and reference checks and sign entrusted-processing agreements with vendors. Collect the prior employer's termination certificate and check non-compete and confidentiality obligations, because hiring someone still bound creates joint liability (LCL Art. 91).

processes.name: Export-control screening for new hires
processes.summary: Ensures no new hire, intern or contractor receives EAR- or ITAR-controlled technology or source code until the release is authorized. Role-based technology classification happens at requisition; person-based screening (U.S.-person status and countries of citizenship or permanent residency) happens after the offer, separately from the I-9, and only for flagged roles. Good looks like zero unlicensed releases, start dates and access gated on clearance, accurate I-129 Part 6 certifications and no citizenship-discrimination exposure.
processes.owner: Trade Compliance (determinations and Technology Control Plan), Talent Acquisition (workflow), Immigration (I-129 Part 6), IT (access gating)
processes.trigger: Offer accepted, or contractor/intern engagement approved, for a position carrying an export-control flag from PL-02; also transfers, new projects and immigration-status changes
outputs: Role technology classification (jurisdiction and ECCNs) on the Darwinbox position
Export questionnaire (separate from the I-9) and determination: no license required, license exception, or license needed
License application and per-person tracking of license provisos
Signed Technology Control Plan (TCP) briefing acknowledgment
Access provisioning ticket tied to export status
I-129 Part 6 analysis kept in the immigration file
processes.sla: Determination within 3 business days of questionnaire; license cases follow BIS processing times (plan for weeks to months; verify current times) with start date or scope adjusted

steps.label: Classify role's technology access
steps.detail: At requisition (PL-02), Trade Compliance and the manager identify what the role will touch (design repositories, EDA projects, foundry PDK and process data, test programs, encryption source), its jurisdiction (EAR or ITAR) and ECCNs, and set the flag on the position. Roles limited to EAR99 or published information stay unflagged.

steps.label: Confirm day-1 and 90-day access scope
steps.detail: Manager lists the specific repositories, projects and lab zones needed on Day 1 and in the first 90 days on a need-to-know basis, and an alternative work plan if a license is needed.

steps.label: Send export questionnaire post-offer
steps.detail: For flagged roles only, after offer acceptance, the export tool sends the same questions to every candidate: 'Are you a U.S. person (citizen, national, lawful permanent resident, asylee or refugee)?' and, if not, all countries of citizenship and current permanent residency. It explains the export purpose, requests no documents and is not linked to the I-9 or E-Verify.
steps.control: Uniform, need-based, post-offer questionnaire (DOJ IER guidance)

steps.label: Complete export questionnaire
steps.detail: Answers are stored in the export tool, not in the Greenhouse profile visible to the hiring team or in I-9 records.

steps.label: Screen against restricted lists
steps.detail: Screen the individual against the Entity List, SDN, Unverified and MEU lists and DOJ DSP covered persons. Prior employment at a listed entity triggers enhanced trade-secret onboarding (TA-10), never rejection by nationality.

steps.label: Determine license requirement
steps.detail: Apply the rules: release in the US to a foreign person is a deemed export to their most recent citizenship or permanent residency; release abroad to a third-country national is a deemed reexport; access by a local national in China, Taiwan or India is an export or reexport to that country. Check reasons for control, license exceptions and published or fundamental-research exclusions, and record the determination.

steps.label: License required?
steps.detail: No license (or a documented exception) clears the hire; a license requirement needs a plan before start.

steps.label: Apply for license or limit scope
steps.detail: Options: file a BIS deemed-export license and align timing; start the person on unflagged work with IT-enforced restrictions; move the start date; or offer an alternate role. For ITAR, a DSP-5 or TAA is needed and China is under a policy of denial. Legal reviews before any offer withdrawal (IER risk).

steps.label: Gate start date and access status
steps.detail: Darwinbox export status (Pending, Cleared, Licensed, Restricted) drives start confirmation; the start date is not confirmed until status is Cleared, Licensed or an approved Restricted plan exists.
steps.control: Flagged hires cannot move to 'Ready to start' without an export status

steps.label: Complete I-129 Part 6 from determination
steps.detail: For H-1B, H-1B1, L-1 and O-1A petitions (new, extension or amendment) the signatory certifies based on Trade Compliance's written determination; if a license is needed, certify that access will be blocked until it is obtained. The analysis lives in the immigration file, not the I-9.
steps.control: Part 6 signed only with the written determination on file

steps.label: Complete TCP briefing and certify
steps.detail: Before or on Day 1, complete the TCP briefing in the LMS (what is controlled, need-to-know, no sharing by chat or screen share, visitor rules, travel with devices) and sign the acknowledgment.

steps.label: Provision access per export status
steps.detail: Identity rules grant repository, EDA project and lab-badge access only when export status and license provisos allow; requests for controlled resources are rejected otherwise and logged.
steps.control: Controlled-resource access requires export status in the identity system

steps.label: Re-screen on changes; keep records
steps.detail: Re-screen on transfer, new project or ECCN, promotion, location change, immigration-status change and license expiry; follow license exit-reporting conditions; keep records 5 years (EAR Part 762).
steps.sla: Within 5 bd of a Darwinbox change

steps.label: Hire cleared; access controlled
steps.detail: Employee starts with access matched to export status; the determination and TCP acknowledgment are on file.

raci.C: Trade Compliance, Head of Talent Acquisition

controls.control: Flagged positions cannot move to 'Ready to start' in Darwinbox without export status Cleared, Licensed or an approved Restricted plan
controls.evidence: Darwinbox status history and weekly exception report

controls.control: Export questionnaire issued only for flagged roles, after offer, with uniform questions, no document requests and storage outside I-9 and ATS records
controls.evidence: Tool configuration and quarterly sample review

controls.control: Access to controlled repositories, EDA projects and lab zones requires export status in the identity system
controls.evidence: Identity policy rule export and access logs

controls.control: I-129 Part 6 signed only with Trade Compliance's written determination on file
controls.evidence: Immigration file checklist

controls.control: Quarterly reconciliation of all users with controlled-resource access against export clearance and license provisos
controls.evidence: Reconciliation report and remediation tickets

controls.control: Annual audit of postings and ATS questions for citizenship restrictions or citizenship knockout questions
controls.evidence: Audit worksheet with fixes

controls.control: Darwinbox events (transfer, location, job code, immigration status) automatically trigger re-screening
controls.evidence: Integration rule and re-screen log

kpis.name: Unlicensed releases found by self-review or audit
kpis.why: The outcome the process exists to prevent.

kpis.name: Determination turnaround
kpis.why: Keeps export screening off the critical path.

kpis.name: Flagged hires with delayed start
kpis.why: Shows license needs are anticipated at req stage.

kpis.name: Access-vs-clearance reconciliation exceptions
kpis.why: Access drift is how most real releases happen.

kpis.name: Recruiters and hiring managers trained on IER-compliant export questions
kpis.why: Untrained questions create citizenship-discrimination exposure.

considerations: Classify the role, then screen the person: technology access is a property of the position, set once in PL-02 and re-checked on change; the person-level question is asked only for flagged positions and only after the offer.

Never use export controls as a hiring filter: the EAR and ITAR require authorization before release, not citizenship-based hiring. 'US citizens only' needs a law, regulation, executive order or government contract behind it; otherwise it is 8 U.S.C. 1324b exposure.

The I-9 is not an export tool: do not ask for passports to establish nationality or route export data through I-9 or E-Verify. Asylees, refugees and lawful permanent residents are U.S. persons for EAR purposes.

'Release' is broad: screen shares, design reviews, Git or Perforce access, EDA project permissions, visual inspection in labs and oral explanation all count. Most real violations happen through collaboration tools, not file transfers.

Deemed reexports follow the technology abroad: a PRC national in Toronto, Hsinchu or Bengaluru working on US-origin controlled technology may need a license even where the item needs none for Canada, Taiwan or India, because BIS looks at most recent citizenship or permanent residency.
Treat contractors, interns, visiting researchers and onsite interview candidates exactly like employees; many near-misses involve interns on design teams and contractors with repository access.

When a license is needed, choose between time, scope and role: many foreign-person engineers can start productively on unflagged work while a license is pending, which beats rescinding the offer (Legal reviews any withdrawal).
Status changes cut both ways: an H-1B engineer who becomes a lawful permanent resident becomes a U.S. person, while a move into China-facing FAE work can bring EAR 744.6 U.S.-person restrictions.
Keep records for five years (EAR Part 762) and track license provisos per person, including any reporting obligation when the person leaves.

variations.how: Same questionnaire and determination; university partners screened against the Entity List; Canadian Mitacs/NSERC projects follow the federal sensitive technology research policy.
Screening before any access; the vendor contract requires cooperation with export screening; access is time-bound (PL-05).

Access by PRC nationals in China to controlled US-origin technology is an export to China; many advanced computing and semiconductor technologies need licenses under restrictive review, so China roles are scoped around unflagged work.

variations.when: Third-country national in Taiwan, India or Canada
variations.how: Deemed reexport analysis to most recent citizenship or permanent residency (e.g., a PRC national in Hsinchu or Toronto).
U.S. persons or licensed foreign persons only; ITAR considers all nationalities and China is under a policy of denial (22 CFR 126.1); separate ITAR TCP and IT enclave.

variations.when: U.S. person supporting China fabs or customers
variations.how: EAR 744.6 review before assignment; no support for development or production at advanced-node PRC fabs without a license.

variations.when: Existing employee changes status or project
variations.how: Re-screen within 5 business days of the Darwinbox change; access adjusted before new project work begins.

countries.us: Releasing EAR-controlled technology or source code to a foreign person in the US is a deemed export to their most recent country of citizenship or permanent residency (15 CFR 734.13(b)); H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN and F-1/OPT holders are foreign persons. Ask export questions only for roles needing controlled access, separately from the I-9, consistent with DOJ IER guidance and 8 U.S.C. 1324b. I-129 Part 6 must reflect Trade Compliance's actual determination for H-1B, H-1B1, L-1 and O-1A petitions, including extensions and amendments.
countries.us-ca: FEHA bars national-origin discrimination, and export licensing justifies citizenship or immigration-status questions only as far as licensing requires, ideally after the offer. California limits E-Verify to what federal law requires and never before an offer, so keep E-Verify out of the export workflow; the cannabis-protection exception covers roles needing federal security clearances.
countries.ca: A foreign national in a Canadian office receiving US-origin controlled chip technology is a deemed reexport judged by most recent citizenship or permanent residency, so a PRC national in Toronto may need a licence. Ontario's Human Rights Code protects citizenship and both provinces protect place of origin, so apply citizenship-based limits only where legally required. ITAR items also bring Canada's Controlled Goods Program registration and security assessments.
countries.in: Release of US-origin controlled technology to Indian nationals in India is a reexport to India (Country Group A:5, often eligible for license exceptions), while release to third-country nationals such as PRC or Russian nationals is a deemed reexport that may need a license under advanced-computing and semiconductor rules. Check India's own SCOMET controls for technology leaving India, and give notice when collecting nationality data (DPDP Act).
countries.tw: EAR deemed-reexport rules apply to foreign-national staff in Taiwan; release to Taiwanese nationals is a reexport to Taiwan, and PRC nationals are effectively barred from working in Taiwan. Check Taiwan's strategic high-tech commodities (SHTC) controls before sharing technology with third parties, and treat roles on national core key technologies (e.g., AI/HPC chip design) as security-sensitive under the National Security Act.
countries.cn: Access by PRC nationals in China to controlled US-origin technology is an export to China, and many advanced computing and semiconductor technologies need licenses under restrictive review, so scope China R&D roles around unflagged work. EAR 744.6 restricts U.S. persons (including green-card holders) from supporting advanced-node PRC fabs; nationality data is personal information under PIPL, and HR communications tied to Entity List compliance should be reviewed for Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law exposure.

processes.name: Immigration sponsorship for new hires
processes.summary: Decides whether and how to sponsor a new hire's work authorization and runs the filing to a lawful start: route selection, cost approval, prevailing wage and LCA, petitions and permits, and start-date alignment. Covers US (H-1B cap and transfers, TN, O-1, L-1, OPT/STEM OPT), Canada (GTS/LMIA, ICT, CUSMA), Taiwan (work permit, Gold Card), China (work permit, Z visa) and India (E visa). Good looks like the route chosen before the offer, no one working without authorization, and current US fee exposure understood at approval.
processes.owner: Immigration (process), Talent Acquisition (candidate), Dept Head (cost approval), Legal (policy)
processes.trigger: Candidate needs employer-sponsored work authorization for the hiring location, identified at screen and confirmed before offer
outputs: Route assessment with cost and timing estimate
Sponsorship approval under POL-19
Filed petitions and permits (LCA and I-129, LMIA/GTS or IRCC offer, WDA permit, China work permit)
Start date aligned to authorization
Expiry and compliance diary in the immigration case system
processes.sla: Route assessment within 3 business days; filing within 10 business days of signed offer, then route-dependent processing

steps.label: Flag sponsorship need at screen
steps.detail: Ask every candidate the same question ('Will you now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status?') and record current status, expiry and prior H-1B cap history; no citizenship questions.

steps.label: Assess route, timing and cost
steps.detail: Compare routes: H-1B transfer, new cap H-1B (March wage-weighted lottery), TN, O-1, L-1 from an affiliate, STEM OPT; Canada GTS, ICT or CUSMA; Taiwan WDA permit or Gold Card; China work permit and Z visa; India E visa. Include current US fee status and proposed fees in the estimate.

steps.label: Approve sponsorship cost?
steps.detail: Dept Head approves cost and timing risk before the offer is extended.

steps.label: Prepare wage and employer filings
steps.detail: US: prevailing wage level, LCA posting and certification, and I-129 Part 6 from TA-06. Canada: GTS LMIA with Labour Market Benefits Plan, or IRCC Employer Portal offer with the C$230 compliance fee. Taiwan: WDA permit. China: work permit application.

steps.label: Provide documents; obtain visa
steps.detail: Candidate provides degrees, evaluations and passports and completes consular or port-of-entry steps; for beneficiaries abroad, re-check the $100K proclamation status at filing.

steps.label: Confirm authorization before start
steps.detail: Approval, visa or permit in hand; STEM OPT hires need an I-983 and an E-Verify employer; OPT hires affected by the F-1 fixed-admission rule may need I-539 and I-765 approvals before starting.

steps.label: Set start date and diary expiries
steps.detail: Start date confirmed in Darwinbox only after authorization; diary permit, visa and I-94 expiries, H-1B maximum stay, LCA public access file and Canadian SIN (starting with 9) expiry.
steps.control: No start date without authorization evidence

steps.label: Authorized start; compliance diaried
steps.detail: Case moves to MV-06 for maintenance and green card planning.

steps.label: Sponsorship declined; candidate told
steps.detail: Candidate informed promptly and consistently with the posting; decision recorded in Greenhouse.

controls.control: No start date confirmed without work authorization evidence reviewed by Immigration
controls.evidence: Approval record in the immigration case system and Darwinbox start gate

controls.control: Sponsorship approved under POL-19 with a cost estimate reflecting current fee status before the offer
controls.evidence: Approval record in Greenhouse and the immigration system

controls.control: Monthly expiry report (permits, visas, I-94, EAD, LCA) with 180/90/60-day alerts
controls.evidence: Expiry report and action log

controls.control: LCA public access file and notice posting completed for every H-1B
controls.evidence: Public access file checklist

kpis.name: Sponsored starts delayed beyond plan
kpis.why: Measures route and timing accuracy.

kpis.name: Work authorization lapses
kpis.why: Lapses mean unlawful employment and forced leave.

kpis.name: Route decided before offer
kpis.why: Prevents offers that cannot convert.

considerations: Decide the route before the offer and make the offer contingent on authorization; discovering after acceptance that a candidate has no viable path is expensive and damages the brand.

H-1B fee status as of Sept 22, 2026: Proclamation 10973's $100,000 payment for beneficiaries abroad or requesting consular notification was vacated nationwide (D. Mass., Jun 8, 2026; 1st Cir. denied a stay Jul 24, 2026) but was extended on Sept 18, 2026 through Sept 21, 2027, and a D.C. Circuit appeal is pending, so it could return quickly if a stay is granted. Change-of-status filings for people already in the US fall outside it; confirm with counsel at filing.

DHS separately proposed a $103,265 fee on every cap-subject H-1B petition (NPRM Aug 25, 2026) for filings from Apr 1, 2027 (FY2028); extensions, amendments, cap-exempt petitions and changes of employer are excluded, so H-1B transfers stay comparatively cheap.

The wage-weighted lottery (effective Feb 27, 2026) gives Level IV registrations 4 entries and Level I one; for strategic new-grad hires, consider offering at a higher wage level. FY2027 drew 211,600 registrations with no second round.

Use the whole portfolio: TN for Canadian and Mexican engineers, O-1 for senior specialists, L-1 after a year at an affiliate (Canada, Taiwan or India hub first), and Canada GTS as a fast alternative when H-1B fails.
Layoffs now affect petitions: the Sept 18, 2026 EO tells agencies to weigh past-year and planned layoffs in LCA and petition adjudication, so coordinate sponsorship with any planned reductions.

variations.how: No lottery; portability can allow start on filing if status is valid; new LCA and Part 6; outside the proposed cap-petition fee.

variations.when: F-1 OPT or STEM OPT new grad
variations.how: STEM OPT needs E-Verify and Form I-983; fixed I-94 end dates since Sept 15, 2026 may require I-539 plus I-765 approvals before start; cap-gap runs to Apr 1 for H-1B change-of-status filers.

variations.when: Canadian or Mexican citizen for a US role
variations.how: TN (CUSMA) for listed professions such as engineer; Canadians can apply at the port of entry; TN is not dual-intent, so plan green card timing carefully.

variations.when: Candidate abroad for the Canada or Taiwan office
variations.how: Canada GTS (10-business-day LMIA standard, about 2-week work permit) or ICT; Taiwan WDA permit or Employment Gold Card.

countries.us: H-1B cap registration is in March under the wage-weighted lottery; the $100K payment for beneficiaries abroad is vacated nationwide but re-proclaimed through Sept 21, 2027, and a $103,265 cap-petition fee is proposed for FY2028 filings. DOL's March 2026 NPRM would raise Level I-IV prevailing wages to the 34th/52nd/70th/88th percentiles, affecting H-1B, E-3 and PERM costs.
countries.us-ca: Use E-Verify only where federal law requires it (e.g., STEM OPT employers), never before an offer, and give employees notice within 72 hours of a federal I-9 inspection notice. Bay Area OEWS wage levels are among the highest in the country, so budget LCA wages accordingly.
countries.ca: Global Talent Stream Category B covers software and computer engineers with a 10-business-day LMIA standard and a Labour Market Benefits Plan; intra-company transfers and CUSMA professionals are LMIA-exempt, with the offer submitted in the IRCC Employer Portal and a C$230 compliance fee. Spousal open work permits now require the principal to be in a TEER 0/1 (or listed TEER 2/3) job with 16+ months left on the permit.
countries.in: Foreign nationals need an Employment (E) visa, generally with salary over USD 25,000/yr, and FRRO registration within 14 days of arrival for stays of 180+ days under the Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025 (verify employer reporting duties). Expatriates contribute to EPF on full salary as international workers, subject to pending litigation.
countries.tw: Obtain a WDA work permit for specialized work (salary threshold currently NT$47,971/month; verify) or use the Employment Gold Card, plus the residence permit (ARC). 2026 Foreign Professionals Act amendments add open permits for top-200 university graduates, spouse work rights and faster permanent residency.
countries.cn: Obtain the Foreigner's Work Permit (A/B/C tiers), Z visa and residence permit within 30 days of entry before any work; foreign employees' contracts are capped at 5 years. Courts recognize employment only for foreigners with permanent residency or valid permits (SPC Interpretation II Art. 4).

processes.name: University & intern hiring
processes.summary: Runs campus recruiting for new graduates and interns or co-ops: school and program selection, a fixed hiring calendar, standardized assessment, cohort offers, intern pay and classification, student work authorization, and conversion to full-time. Covers US, Canadian co-op, Indian campus, Taiwanese and Chinese university channels. Good looks like calibrated cohort hiring on schedule, paid internships that meet local wage and student-status rules, and export- and FCPA-safe selection and access.
processes.owner: University Recruiting (Talent Acquisition), Hiring Managers (projects), L&D (program), Legal (student-status and pay rules)
processes.trigger: Approved evergreen or campus requisitions from PL-02 under the annual campus plan
outputs: Campus plan (schools, programs, headcount by site)
Standard assessments and hiring-committee decisions
Cohort offers and intern agreements
Intern project plans with export-control clearance
Return-offer and conversion decisions
processes.sla: Offer within 10 business days of final interview; return-offer decisions by the last week of the internship

steps.label: Set campus plan and school list
steps.detail: Select schools and programs by site (e.g., Waterloo/Toronto/UBC co-op, IITs and IISc, NTU/NTHU/NYCU, Tsinghua/Fudan/SJTU) with outreach open to all; screen research partners against the Entity List.

steps.label: Run assessments and interviews
steps.detail: Standard online assessment (AI-tool governance per TA-03) and structured interviews with the campus scorecard.

steps.label: Calibrate in hiring committee
steps.detail: Cross-site committee calibrates levels, locations and offers so equivalent candidates get equivalent outcomes.

steps.label: Confirm pay, status and export
steps.detail: Interns are paid at least local minimum wage with overtime rules applied (no unpaid internships); student authorization confirmed (CPT/OPT, Canadian co-op permit, China school internship agreement); flagged projects cleared through TA-06.

steps.label: Extend cohort offers with deadlines
steps.detail: Standard packages with reasonable response deadlines (2-3 weeks); housing or relocation stipends within POL-31 and local law.

steps.label: Accept and complete pre-start steps
steps.detail: Background checks (TA-05), export questionnaire (TA-06) and work authorization (TA-07) completed before the start date.

steps.label: Run intern program and evaluations
steps.detail: Onboarding, mentor, a project with defined deliverables, and midpoint and final evaluations on competencies; lab safety training is completed before any lab access.

steps.label: Return offer?
steps.detail: Decision based on the final evaluation and the next year's campus plan.

steps.label: Extend return or full-time offer
steps.detail: Return offers use the new-grad package and go through TA-04 approvals.

steps.label: Internship closed; conversion logged
steps.detail: Outcome and feedback recorded; cohort metrics feed next year's plan.

raci.activity: Intern pay, classification and student-status compliance

controls.control: No unpaid internships; intern pay at or above local minimum wage and overtime-eligible where required
controls.evidence: Intern pay table approved by Legal and Total Rewards

controls.control: Intern projects touching flagged technology cleared through TA-06 before start
controls.evidence: Export determination record per intern

controls.control: Internships are open-application only; no customer- or official-requested placements
controls.evidence: Program criteria and Compliance review log

kpis.name: New-grad offer acceptance
kpis.why: Measures campus brand and offer competitiveness.

kpis.name: Return-offer acceptance
kpis.why: Interns are the cheapest, best-assessed pipeline.

kpis.name: Starts delayed by student status or authorization
kpis.why: Tests calendar planning against immigration rules.

considerations: Treat interns as hourly, non-exempt employees in every country; this settles the unpaid-intern debate and keeps overtime and break rules straight (California's exempt floor is far above intern pay).

Build the calendar around student status: OPT and STEM OPT start dates can slip under the F-1 fixed-admission rule (effective Sept 15, 2026), Canadian co-op students need co-op work permits, and Chinese student interns generally use school-backed internship agreements rather than labor contracts.

Interns are frequent deemed-export cases: foreign-national interns on design teams get the same TA-06 screening as employees, and university partners are screened against the Entity List and Canada's sensitive technology research list.
Keep programs open to all: race- or sex-restricted internships and fellowships are high-risk after EO 14173 and Ames; broad outreach to many schools is fine.
Internships requested by customers, SOE officials or university officials tied to procurement are a classic FCPA 'thing of value'; keep internships open-application only.

variations.how: Student hired under an approved co-op program; check ESA student rules; SR&ED time coding; Mitacs-funded projects follow research-security policy.
Offers made months before joining; appointment letter at joining; any bond or joining-bonus clawback limited to reasonable liquidated damages.
School-backed internship agreement, internship allowance and accident insurance; not a labor contract (verify local rules).

countries.us: Pay interns as non-exempt employees under the FLSA, and ensure STEM OPT hires meet E-Verify and Form I-983 training-plan requirements. Demographically restricted internships create Title VII and False Claims Act exposure (IBM $17M settlement, Apr 2026).
countries.us-ca: Interns earn at least the state or higher local minimum wage (e.g., Sunnyvale $19.50, Mountain View $19.70 in 2026) with daily overtime and meal and rest breaks. Housing or relocation stipends cannot carry repayment terms for agreements entered on or after Jan 1, 2026 (AB 692).
countries.ca: Ontario's minimum wage rises to C$17.95 on Oct 1, 2026 and BC's is C$18.25; students on approved college or university co-op programs may fall outside some ESA rules (verify per program). Mitacs and NSERC collaborations follow the federal Policy on Sensitive Technology Research and Affiliations of Concern.
countries.in: Campus hires are often 'workers' under the Labour Codes; issue appointment letters at joining and keep training bonds or joining-bonus clawbacks reasonable and pro-rated (Supreme Court upheld a reasonable bond in 2025). Verify minimum-wage and apprenticeship rules for stipend interns.
countries.tw: Interns in an employment relationship are LSA-covered at the NT$29,500/month or NT$196/hour minimum with labor insurance. 2026 Foreign Professionals Act amendments open work permits for graduates of top-200 universities.
countries.cn: Full-time students on internships are generally not employees; use a school-backed internship agreement with an allowance and accident insurance (verify local rules). Graduates hired on labor contracts need probation matched to the contract term and social insurance from Day 1.

processes.name: Executive hiring
processes.summary: Governs hiring of VPs and executive officers from search through announcement and onboarding into public-company obligations. Covers retained search, CEO and Comp Committee approval of pay, 8-K Item 5.02 disclosure for covered officers, Section 16 and insider onboarding, the D&O questionnaire, clawback acknowledgment and Nasdaq inducement grants. Good looks like no surprises: pay approved by the right body, filings on time, and the executive trading-compliant from Day 1.
processes.owner: CHRO (process), Comp Committee (pay approval), Legal and Corporate Secretary (disclosure and Section 16)
processes.trigger: Approved VP+ or officer requisition (PL-02), or board-led CEO or officer succession
outputs: Search firm contract and position specification
Comp Committee-approved package (base, bonus, equity, severance/CIC terms)
Executed offer or employment agreement drafted as if public
8-K Item 5.02 filing and press release (plus inducement grant announcement if used)
Section 16 and insider onboarding pack: Form 3, power of attorney, EDGAR Next access, D&O questionnaire, insider designation, clawback acknowledgment
processes.sla: Package approval within 5 business days of finalist; 8-K within 4 business days of the decision; Form 3 within 10 days of becoming an officer

steps.label: Define role spec and engage search
steps.detail: Agree the specification and assessment plan; contract the search firm (fee, guarantee, off-limits terms reviewed by Legal); involve the board for CEO direct reports and officer roles.

steps.label: Run search and structured assessment
steps.detail: Structured leadership interviews, CEO and board panels, consented referencing, executive background checks (TA-05), conflict and related-person checks (TA-10) and review of prior restrictive covenants.

steps.label: Select finalist and propose terms
steps.detail: CEO proposes base, target bonus, equity (plan or inducement), and severance and change-in-control terms under the executive policy, benchmarked by the compensation consultant with 280G, 162(m) and 409A effects modeled.

steps.label: Approve compensation package?
steps.detail: Independent directors approve officer pay and all equity; the CEO is not present for decisions on CEO pay.

steps.label: Draft agreement and disclosure plan
steps.detail: Draft as if it will be filed (Item 601(b)(10)): clawback, protected-rights carve-outs, no excise-tax gross-ups; assess 8-K Item 5.02(c)/(e), Reg FD timing and any Nasdaq 5635(c)(4) inducement grant (independent approval, prompt press release).

steps.label: Extend offer and obtain signature
steps.detail: CHRO and CEO extend the offer; signature triggers the disclosure clock if it was not already running from the board decision.

steps.label: File 8-K and announce
steps.detail: File within 4 business days of the decision or appointment with biography, related-person interests and material terms; coordinate press release, employee and customer communications.

steps.label: Complete Section 16 and insider setup
steps.detail: Form 3 within 10 days, power of attorney and EDGAR Next Login.gov credentials, insider list and blackout calendar, pre-clearance, D&O questionnaire, clawback acknowledgment and grant processing on the approved date.
steps.control: Section 16 onboarding checklist completed before the first open window

steps.label: Executive onboarded as insider
steps.detail: Executive moves to ON-01/ON-04 with public-company obligations in place.

controls.control: Executive officer pay and all equity approved by the Comp Committee before the offer; CEO absent for CEO pay decisions
controls.evidence: Committee minutes and resolutions

controls.control: HR notifies Legal the same day an officer decision is made; the 8-K deadline runs from the decision date
controls.evidence: Disclosure checklist with timestamps and filed 8-K

controls.control: Section 16 onboarding checklist completed before the first trading window
controls.evidence: Completed checklist and signed acknowledgments

controls.control: Inducement grants only to bona fide new hires, approved by independent directors and announced by press release
controls.evidence: Inducement checklist, press release and Form S-8 record

kpis.name: 8-K and Form 3 filed on time
kpis.why: Late filings are publicly disclosed and invite SEC attention.

kpis.name: Finalist to signed offer
kpis.why: Executive candidates have alternatives and counteroffers.

kpis.name: Executive retention at 24 months
kpis.why: Tests search and assessment quality.

considerations: Start the disclosure clock at the decision, not the start date: 8-K Item 5.02 runs 4 business days from when the appointment is decided or the officer gives notice, so the press release and communications plan must be ready before the offer.
Draft every officer agreement as if it will be filed and read by proxy advisors: avoid excise-tax gross-ups, single-trigger change-in-control vesting and guaranteed bonuses.

Inducement grants (Nasdaq 5635(c)(4)) allow grants outside the shareholder-approved plan to genuine new hires, but only with independent approval and a prompt press release; they do not fix a thin plan reserve.

Executives from competitors bring trade-secret and covenant risk; get the clean-hire certification and prior-agreement review before the offer (TA-10). California voids non-competes but not trade-secret claims.
Add the executive to the insider list, blackout calendar and pre-clearance before their first window; officers adopting 10b5-1 plans face a 90-120 day cooling-off.
From tax years starting in 2027, 162(m) also covers the five highest-paid other employees each year, so large sign-on awards to senior non-officer hires can lose deductibility; model them.

variations.how: Board-led search and full board approval; Comp Committee sets pay with its consultant; 8-K 5.02(c) and (e); Section 16 onboarding; D&O insurer notified.

variations.when: VP who is not an executive officer
variations.how: No 8-K or Section 16, but insider designation and pre-clearance under the insider trading policy; the Comp Committee or its delegate approves equity.
Local employment contract plus the US award agreement; Ontario C-suite non-compete exception; China and Taiwan non-compete compensation rules; tax equalization if relocating (MV-02).

countries.us: Covered officer appointments (PEO, president, PFO, PAO, COO, NEOs) need an 8-K within 4 business days with biography, related-person interests and material compensation terms (Item 5.02(c)/(e)); Section 16 officers file Form 3 within 10 days and Form 4 within 2 business days using EDGAR Next credentials. Clawback acknowledgment (Rule 10D-1, Nasdaq 5608) and Item 404 related-person review also apply.
countries.us-ca: Executives cannot be bound by non-competes, and non-California law or forum clauses are valid only if the executive was individually represented by counsel in negotiating the agreement (LC 925). AB 692 bars repayment clauses for agreements from Jan 1, 2026 (verify AB 1697 outcome).
countries.ca: Ontario's non-compete ban has a C-suite exception, and common-law reasonable notice for senior executives can approach 24 months unless an enforceable termination clause limits it. Equity forfeiture terms must expressly exclude the notice period (Matthews).
countries.in: Post-employment non-competes are void even for executives (Contract Act s.27), so rely on garden leave and confidentiality. Parent RSUs are taxed as perquisites at vesting with Indian TDS, and executives must report foreign equity in Schedule FA.
countries.tw: Only true mandated managers appointed under the Company Act fall outside the LSA; most executives are LSA-covered employees. A post-exit non-compete must pay at least 50% of average monthly wage for up to 2 years (LSA Art. 9-1).
countries.cn: Senior management may be bound by non-competes of up to 2 years with monthly post-exit compensation of at least 30% of prior average pay; foreign executives need an A-tier work permit before starting. RSUs need SAFE Circular 7 registration and IIT withholding at vesting.

processes.name: Rehire, relatives & conflict screening
processes.summary: Screens finalists before offer for conflicts that create legal, governance or IP risk: rehire eligibility, relatives in the reporting chain or related-person transactions, connections to government officials, SOEs or customers (FCPA), and prior-employer restrictive covenants and trade secrets. Good looks like every flag reviewed by the right function before offer, documented mitigations, and a clean-hire certification signed by every new hire.
processes.owner: Talent Acquisition (questionnaire), Ethics & Compliance (FCPA and conflicts), Legal (restrictive covenants and Item 404)
processes.trigger: Candidate reaches the final stage, or a rehire or relative flag appears in Greenhouse or Darwinbox
outputs: Candidate disclosure questionnaire (relatives, official or customer connections, prior agreements, outside activities)
Rehire eligibility result
Compliance and Legal review memo for flagged cases
Clean-hire (no-bring) certification
Documented mitigations (reporting-line change, recusal, access walls)
processes.sla: Flag reviews completed within 3 business days

steps.label: Send disclosure questionnaire
steps.detail: At the final stage, every candidate gets the same questions: relatives at the company; relationships with government officials, SOE employees, customers or suppliers; prior agreements (NDA, non-compete, non-solicit); outside activities and investments; prior employment with the company.

steps.label: Complete disclosures; share agreements
steps.detail: Candidate answers and provides copies of restrictive-covenant agreements, redacting any confidential business information.

steps.label: Check rehire eligibility
steps.detail: Check the OF-10 rehire code and prior separation reason in Darwinbox; 'not eligible' goes to HRBP review.

steps.label: Any flags?
steps.detail: Flags include relatives, official or customer connections, restrictive covenants, competitor or Entity List prior employer, and rehire concerns.

steps.label: Review FCPA and relative conflicts
steps.detail: Confirm the hire is merit-based with no link to business with the connected official or customer; relatives cannot be in the same reporting chain or influence pay or hiring; relatives of directors or officers earning over $120,000 go to Legal for Item 404 and audit committee review.

steps.label: Review covenants and trade-secret risk
steps.detail: Assess enforceability of prior non-competes and non-solicits by jurisdiction, and trade-secret exposure; decide on start-date deferral, role scoping or access walls for the first months.

steps.label: Risk acceptable with mitigations?
steps.detail: HRBP, Legal and Compliance agree mitigations (reporting change, recusal, access walls) and record them in the case file.

steps.label: Sign clean-hire certification
steps.detail: Candidate certifies they will bring no prior-employer confidential information, have returned or deleted it, and will not use it; the certification is part of the offer package.

steps.label: Cleared to offer (TA-04)
steps.detail: Clearance and any mitigations are attached to the offer approval.

steps.label: Do not proceed; reason documented
steps.detail: Candidate is declined with a documented, non-discriminatory reason; records retained.

raci.activity: FCPA review of official, SOE and customer connections

controls.control: Offer creation blocked while a disclosure flag is open
controls.evidence: Greenhouse flag status and review memo

controls.control: Hires connected to government officials, SOEs or customers approved by Compliance before offer; records kept 5 years
controls.evidence: Compliance approval record

controls.control: Every hire signs a clean-hire certification before Day 1
controls.evidence: E-signature record

controls.control: Annual report of employed relatives of directors and officers for the proxy (Item 404)
controls.evidence: Report and audit committee minutes

kpis.name: Flags resolved within 3 business days
kpis.why: Screening must not stall offers.

kpis.name: Hires with signed clean-hire certification
kpis.why: Core evidence of reasonable trade-secret measures.

kpis.name: Undisclosed relative or conflict cases found after hire
kpis.why: Tests questionnaire effectiveness.

considerations: Ask everyone the same questions at the same stage; ad hoc 'are you related to anyone here?' questions invite marital or family-status claims and miss the cases that matter.

FCPA risk sits in referrals and internships as much as senior hires: Qualcomm ($7.5M, 2016) and JPMorgan (about $264M, 2016) involved hiring relatives of officials. DOJ's June 2025 guidelines narrowed priorities, but the statute, SEC books-and-records rules and local anti-bribery laws still apply.

Relatives rules should target supervision, audit and payroll conflicts rather than impose a blanket ban: no direct or indirect reporting, no influence over pay or hiring, and disclosure of relationships.

Hiring from competitors is where trade-secret suits start: review prior agreements before offer, require the no-bring certification and wall off sensitive projects for the first months (clean-room onboarding).
Prior employment at an Entity List company triggers enhanced trade-secret and export onboarding, never a nationality-based decision.

variations.how: Check OF-10 rehire code, separation reason and prior investigations; apply China and Taiwan service-continuity and seniority rules; apply equity plan rehire terms.

variations.when: Relative of a director or executive officer
variations.how: Legal and audit committee review before offer; pay over $120,000 disclosed under Item 404.

variations.when: Candidate under an enforceable paid non-compete (Taiwan Art. 9-1 or China)
variations.how: Legal decides on start deferral or role scoping; never induce breach; document the decision.

countries.us: FCPA books-and-records and internal-control provisions reach hiring decisions, and Item 404 requires disclosure when a director's or officer's immediate family member earns over $120,000. Non-competes are void in CA, ND, OK, MN and WY (WA from Jun 30, 2027), but DTSA trade-secret claims follow the candidate.
countries.us-ca: Out-of-state non-competes are void for California employees (B&P 16600.5), yet CUTSA still protects the former employer's trade secrets, so the clean-hire certification matters. Marital status is FEHA-protected, so relatives rules should rest on supervision, security or conflict concerns rather than marriage itself.
countries.ca: Ontario's Human Rights Code lets employers decline to hire the spouse, child or parent of an employee (s.24(1)(d)), while BC protects family and marital status, so apply one supervision-based rule consistently. Ontario non-competes are void below the C-suite and BC courts rarely enforce them.
countries.in: Post-employment non-competes are void (Contract Act s.27), but confidentiality and reasonable non-solicits are enforceable; confirm the relieving letter and notice completion or buy-out. The Prevention of Corruption Act (as amended in 2018) makes companies liable for giving undue advantage to public servants, which covers jobs for officials' relatives.
countries.tw: Have hires from TSMC, MediaTek, UMC and similar firms certify they bring no prior-employer materials, and check any Art. 9-1 non-compete and paid restraint. Corporate liability under the Trade Secrets Act and the 2026 NT$150M TEL penalty show why documented prevention matters.
countries.cn: Collect the prior employer's termination certificate and check non-compete and confidentiality obligations, because hiring someone still bound creates joint liability (LCL Art. 91). Employees of SOE customers can be foreign officials under the FCPA, so hiring their relatives needs Compliance review, and commercial bribery rules under the AUCL also apply.

processes.name: Candidate privacy & data retention
processes.summary: Governs collection, use, cross-border transfer, access and deletion of candidate data in Greenhouse, sourcing tools, assessment vendors and background vendors. Covers notices at collection, consent where required, jurisdictional retention schedules, candidate rights requests and talent-pool consent. Good looks like a notice shown before any data is collected, retention and anonymization automated in Greenhouse, and cross-border transfers from China, India and Taiwan on a lawful basis.
processes.owner: Legal (Privacy) as policy owner; TA Operations as process and ATS configuration owner
processes.trigger: Candidate data is collected (application, sourcing, referral, agency submission) or a retention or rights event occurs
outputs: Jurisdictional candidate privacy notices (CCPA, PIPL, DPDP-ready, PDPA, BC PIPA)
Consent records (PIPL separate consent for cross-border and sensitive data; talent-pool consent)
Greenhouse retention and anonymization rules by jurisdiction
Rights-request log and responses
Vendor processing agreements and privacy risk assessments (PIPIA, CPPA)
processes.sla: Notice at or before collection; rights requests within statutory deadlines (CCPA 45 days); retention jobs run monthly

steps.label: Submit application or profile
steps.detail: Candidate applies, is sourced, referred or submitted by an agency.

steps.label: Present notice; capture consents
steps.detail: Greenhouse shows the jurisdictional notice before submission and captures separate consents where required (PIPL cross-border and sensitive data, talent pool); sourced candidates get the notice at first contact.

steps.label: Process under data agreements
steps.detail: Assessment, background and agency vendors process only under signed terms (CCPA service-provider terms, PIPL entrusted processing, DPDP-ready processor terms) with data location, security and deletion obligations.

steps.label: Assess transfers and risky processing
steps.detail: Run the PIPIA and select the PIPL transfer mechanism for China data sent to the US-hosted ATS, complete CPPA risk assessments for AI and ADMT tools, and track Taiwan PDPC cross-border rules.

steps.label: Candidate hired?
steps.detail: Hired candidates' data moves to the employee record; others stay under candidate retention rules.

steps.label: Move hire data to Darwinbox
steps.detail: Relevant data moves to the Darwinbox personnel file under the employee notice; background and export records stay in separate restricted stores.

steps.label: Apply retention and deletion rules
steps.detail: Greenhouse anonymizes records at the end of the jurisdictional period unless a legal hold applies (e.g., CA 4 years, Ontario 3 years, US federal minimum 1 year, China and India minimum necessary); talent-pool consents are refreshed or data deleted.
steps.control: Monthly retention job with exception report

steps.label: Handle candidate rights requests
steps.detail: Verify identity and respond to access, correction and deletion requests within deadlines, explaining any statutory retention or legal-hold exception.

steps.label: Data retained or deleted on schedule
steps.detail: Retention, deletion and request outcomes logged for audit.

controls.control: Applications cannot be submitted without the jurisdictional notice displayed and required consents captured
controls.evidence: Greenhouse configuration export and consent logs

controls.control: Monthly retention job report (records anonymized, holds applied, failures)
controls.evidence: Job logs and exception tickets

controls.control: No new recruiting vendor or tool without a data agreement, security review and (China) entrusted-processing agreement and PIPIA
controls.evidence: Vendor file under DS-06

controls.control: Annual review of the retention schedule against law changes (e.g., DPDP from May 2027, CA ADS records)
controls.evidence: Retention schedule version log

kpis.name: Rights requests answered within deadline
kpis.why: Statutory deadlines carry penalties and complaints.

kpis.name: Candidate records past retention not anonymized
kpis.why: Over-retention is the most common HR privacy finding.

kpis.name: Recruiting vendors with signed data agreements
kpis.why: Most candidate data sits with vendors.

considerations: Retain long enough to defend, not forever: California's 4-year rule for applications and ADS data is a practical global ceiling for litigation defense; use shorter periods where law requires minimization (China, India) and legal holds for disputes.
Talent pools need consent and refresh: silver-medalist pools are valuable in a tight chip market, but PIPL and DPDP require purpose-limited consent, so re-consent annually or delete.

China candidate data sent to a US-hosted ATS needs a PIPL notice, separate consent for cross-border transfer, a PIPIA and the right mechanism for the volume; keep Chinese background-check data in China where possible.
Keep export questionnaire answers, background reports and voluntary self-ID out of the hiring team's view in Greenhouse; restrict access by role, not convenience.
AI tools create records too: California requires ADS inputs and outputs to be kept 4 years, NYC LL144 bias-audit summaries must be published, and CCPA ADMT notices start Jan 1, 2027.

variations.how: Relevant data moves to Darwinbox under the employee privacy notice; interview notes follow candidate retention rules; background and export data stay in separate restricted stores.
Retention job suspended for affected reqs and candidates (ER-09) until Legal releases the hold.
Delete unless a retention law or hold applies; California and Ontario retention duties override deletion requests, and the candidate is told why.

countries.us: Keep applications and hiring records at least 1 year after the record or action (29 CFR 1602.14), longer once a charge is filed. NYC LL144 requires published bias-audit summaries and notices, and biometric laws such as IL BIPA apply to video-interview or biometric tools.
countries.us-ca: Give a CCPA notice at collection at or before collecting applicant data, including via ATS vendors, stating categories, purposes and retention periods, and honor applicant rights requests (Civ. Code 1798.100). Keep applications, personnel records and ADS data for 4 years (Gov Code 12946; CRD regulations).
countries.ca: Ontario employers with 25+ employees keep job postings, application forms and interview-outcome notices for 3 years. BC PIPA allows reasonable collection for recruitment with notice; PIPEDA does not cover Ontario employee data, and Bill C-36 (tabled June 15, 2026) may change federal rules.
countries.in: Until the DPDP Act's main duties start on 13 May 2027, the IT Act s.43A and SPDI Rules apply; build notice, consent and erasure once the purpose is served (keeping processing logs at least 1 year) into the ATS now. CERT-In requires cyber incidents to be reported within 6 hours.
countries.tw: The PDPA requires notice at collection and written consent or a statutory basis for sensitive data such as criminal records and health; the 2025 amendments create the PDPC and mandatory breach reporting once the Executive Yuan sets the effective date. Draft rules propose 72-hour breach reporting for sensitive data (verify final rules).
countries.cn: PIPL requires a candidate privacy notice, consent for background and reference checks, separate consent for cross-border transfer and sensitive PI, and a PIPIA kept at least 3 years; the transfer mechanism depends on volume (standard contract or certification for 100,000-1M individuals' PI; verify exemptions for smaller volumes). Keep candidate data only for the minimum necessary period.
